definition_zh: 王子；亲王；君主；一方之主；（某领域的）巨子
definition_en: the son of a king or queen, or the male ruler of a small state; also a leading man in a particular activity
core_image: 披着斗篷的年轻人站在王座下一级台阶上
scene: 老国王病重，宫廷内侍捧着王冠站在长廊尽头，等着那位年轻的继承人前来。The young prince rode through the gate with his guard behind him.
sceneCN: 这里 prince 是「王子」（第 1 个义项：君主之子）；句意为年轻的王子在卫队随行下骑马穿过城门。图中可辨识物件：王冠、长廊、马与卫队。

pos.zh: 王子；亲王；君主；一方之主；巨子

collocations.zh: 童话中的白马王子；理想中的男子
威尔士亲王（英国王位继承人的称号）

derivatives.zh: 由 prince 加 -ly 构成，义为「王子的；如王子般慷慨的」
由 prince 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，义为「公主；王妃」
由拉丁语 princeps 的词干加 -ality 构成，义为「公国；侯国」

senses.title: The son of a monarch
senses.definition: a man or boy who is the son of a king or queen, or a close male member of a royal family
senses.definitionCN: 国王或女王之子，或王室中关系亲近的男性成员
senses.example: The prince will take the throne when his mother steps down.
senses.exampleCN: 等母亲退位，这位王子将继承王位。
senses.why: Princeps named the man who took first place in the Roman state, and the title settled on the heir who stands first in line for the crown.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 princeps 本指在罗马政权中占第一位的人，这个称号后来落到继承序列里排第一的继承人身上，于是有了「王子」。

senses.title: The ruler of a small state
senses.definition: a royal title held by the male ruler of a principality or by a noble of the highest rank
senses.definitionCN: 授予小国男性统治者或最高等级贵族的王室称号
senses.example: The prince ruled the mountain valley for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位亲王统治那个山谷四十年。
senses.why: Before it meant an heir, the word meant the man who actually held first place in a territory, so it still names the lords of small states.
senses.whyCN: 在指继承人之前，这个词先指真正在一方土地上占据首位的人，所以今天仍用来称呼小国之主。

senses.title: A leading figure in a field
senses.definition: a man who is outstanding in a particular art, trade or profession
senses.definitionCN: 在某一技艺、行业或职业中极为出众的男子
senses.example: He was hailed as the prince of pianists in his day.
senses.exampleCN: 在他那个年代，他被称为钢琴家中的泰斗。
senses.why: If first place can be held in a state, it can also be held in an art, so the title drifted from political rank to personal prestige.
senses.whyCN: 既然首位可以在一个国家里占据，也就能在一门技艺里占据，于是这个称号从政治等级滑向了个人声望。

intro.en: Prince descends from a Latin compound that joins first with take, so the word has always meant the man who occupies the front position.
intro.cn: prince 出自一个把「第一」和「取」合起来的拉丁语复合词，所以这个词一直指占据最前位置的那个人。

items.en: Primus, the Latin adjective for first, supplied the front half of the compound.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 primus 意为「第一」，为这个复合词提供了前半截。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize; in compounds it appears as -ceps, so the whole word pictures taking the first place.
items.cn: capere 意为「取、抓」，在复合词中写作 -ceps，整个词因此描绘出「占取第一位」的画面。

items.en: Princeps named the leading man of the Roman Senate and later the emperor himself.
items.cn: princeps 指罗马元老院中居首位的人，后来也指皇帝本人。

items.en: Old French prince narrowed the title to a ruler of high rank and to the son of a king.
items.cn: 古法语 prince 把这个称号收窄到高级统治者与国王之子。

items.en: English prince covers the monarch's son, the lord of a principality, and by extension a leading man in any field.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prince 既指君主之子、公国君主，也引申指任何领域中的领军人物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the prince family; the near-meaning group gathers titles for rulers and nobles.
note.cn: 形近组收 prince 这一词族；近义组收表示统治者与贵族的称号。

entries.definition: The female counterpart of a prince, by birth or by marriage.
entries.definitionCN: prince 的女性对应称号，因出生或婚姻而获得。

entries.definition: Belonging to a prince, or generous in the manner of one.
entries.definitionCN: 属于王子的；像王子般慷慨的。

entries.definition: A small state ruled by a prince.
entries.definitionCN: 由亲王统治的小国；公国。

entries.definition: First in rank or importance; also the head of a school.
entries.definitionCN: 等级或重要性第一的；也指校长。

entries.definition: A king, queen or other single ruler of a state.
entries.definitionCN: 国王、女王等一国之君。

entries.definition: A person who governs a country or region.
entries.definitionCN: 统治一个国家或地区的人。

entries.definition: A person of high social rank by birth.
entries.definitionCN: 出身高贵的贵族。

entries.definition: A noble of the highest rank below a prince in some systems.
entries.definitionCN: 某些制度中仅次于亲王的最高等级贵族。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the Latin adjective for first to the verb for taking, and the whole family keeps that picture of seizing the front place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语「第一」的形容词与「取」的动词拼在一起，整族词都保留着「占取最前位置」的画面。

normal.en: Princeps is primus plus capere: the one who takes the first place, which is why prince means both heir and ruler.
normal.cn: princeps 是 primus 加 capere，即「占取第一位的人」，所以 prince 既指继承人也指统治者。

normal.en: Prime and prince share the same opening, so both point at rank one; only the tail differs, and that tail is about taking.
normal.cn: prime 与 prince 开头相同，都指向第一位；区别只在后半截，而后半截讲的是「取」。

normal.en: Prince Charming is the prince of fairy tales, the man who arrives to close the story.
normal.cn: Prince Charming 是童话里的那位王子，故事靠他出场收尾。

normal.en: A crown prince is the heir standing closest to the throne.
normal.cn: crown prince 是离王位最近的那位继承人。

normal.en: The Prince of Wales is a title for the heir to the British throne, not a separate country.
normal.cn: the Prince of Wales 是英国王位继承人的称号，并不是另一个国家。

abstract.en: A prince is first place made visible: a person standing one step below a throne.
abstract.cn: 王子就是「第一位」的可见形态：一个人站在王座下一级台阶上。

abstract.en: Because the word is built from taking, it carries an edge that birth alone does not: the prince is the one who seizes the front.
abstract.cn: 由于这个词由「取」构成，它带着一种单靠出身得不到的锋利：王子是主动占住最前位置的人。

abstract.en: The same title slides from heir to ruler to master of an art, each of them first in their own circle.
abstract.cn: 同一个称号从继承人滑到统治者，再滑到技艺的宗师，每一个都在自己的圈子里排第一。

examples.en: The prince greeted the villagers from the steps of the palace.
examples.cn: 王子在宫殿台阶上向村民致意。

examples.en: The prince of that region signed a treaty with the neighbouring king.
examples.cn: 那一地区的亲王与邻国国王签订了条约。

examples.en: He was the prince of storytellers in that small town.
examples.cn: 在那座小镇上，他是说故事的人里的头一号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普林斯」——英文姓氏 Prince 音译作「普林斯」，记住这个词本来就是王子、亲王。

root: 拉丁语 princeps 由 primus（第一）加 capere（取）构成，经古法语 prince 进入英语；与 prime 同出 primus，但 prince 多出的 -ceps 表示「取」，所以本义是「占第一位的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the one who takes first place; the senses then spread from the heir of a crown to the ruler of a small state and to a leading man in any field.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「占第一位的人」；义项由此从王位继承人，分到小国之主，再到任何领域中的领军者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young man in a cloak standing one step below a throne.
core.cn: 核心意象：披斗篷的年轻人站在王座下一级台阶上。

branches.en: a young heir standing one step below the throne
branches.cn: 年轻的继承人站在王座下一级

branches.en: a crowd bowing as the heir rides through the gate
branches.cn: 继承人骑马穿门而过，人群躬身

branches.en: a mountain valley governed from a single castle
branches.cn: 一座城堡治理着整个山谷

branches.en: a title held by the lord of a small state
branches.cn: 一位小国之主持有的称号

branches.en: a pianist praised as first among his peers
branches.cn: 被赞为同辈第一的钢琴家

intro.en: The word is a Latin compound of first and take, shortened in French, and later fitted with English endings for the quality, the female form and the territory.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「第一」与「取」的复合词，在法语里缩短，后来再加上英语词尾，分别表示性质、女性形态与领地。

latinIntro.en: Latin princeps is built from primus, first, and the -ceps shape of capere, to take; the same primus also stands behind prime.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 princeps 由 primus（第一）与 capere（取）的复合形态 -ceps 构成；同一个 primus 也支撑着 prime。

definition_zh: 印刷；印出；打印；打印件；版画；印记；出版；刊登
definition_en: to put words or pictures onto paper with ink and a press; to make a paper copy from a computer; a mark left by pressure; a picture taken from a prepared plate
core_image: 油墨压上纸面，字从凸起的铅字里翻出来
scene: 窗外雨声不停，车间里的机器一下一下压着纸，油墨味顺着门缝散出去。Every morning the shop would print the day's notices for the whole town.
sceneCN: 这里 print 是「印刷、印出」（第 1 个义项：把油墨压到纸上）；句意为这家店每天早上为全镇印当天的通告。图中可辨识物件：压纸的机器、油墨、门缝。

pos.zh: 印刷；印出；打印；出版；刊登
印刷；印出的字；打印件；版画；印记；指纹

derivatives.zh: 由 print 加 -er 构成，义为「印刷工；打印机」
由 print 加 -ing 构成，义为「印刷；印刷术」
由 print 加 -able 构成，义为「可印刷的；适合刊登的」
由前缀 im-（进入）加 print 构成，义为「压印；留下印记」

senses.title: To press ink onto paper
senses.definition: to produce words or pictures on paper by pressing an inked surface against it
senses.definitionCN: 用蘸了油墨的印版压向纸面，从而产生文字或图像
senses.example: The old press can print a thousand sheets in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这台老印刷机一小时能印一千张。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning to press, so the action begins as pressure on an inked surface rather than as writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自表示「压」的动词，所以这个动作的起点是把蘸墨的表面压下去，而不是拿笔去写。

senses.title: To make a copy from a computer
senses.definition: to send a document from a computer to a machine that puts it on paper; also the paper copy so produced
senses.definitionCN: 把电脑里的文件送到机器上输出到纸上；也指这样得到的纸质件
senses.example: Could you print two copies of the report for the meeting?
senses.exampleCN: 你能把报告打印两份带到会上吗？
senses.why: When computers entered the office, the same pressing action was handed to a printer, so the old verb was reused for the new machine.
senses.whyCN: 电脑进入办公室之后，同样的「压」交给打印机去完成，于是旧动词被直接借来指这台新机器干的事。

senses.title: A picture made from a plate
senses.definition: a picture produced by pressing an inked block, plate or screen onto paper, usually as one of a set
senses.definitionCN: 用蘸墨的木板、金属版或丝网压在纸上得到的图画，通常成套制作
senses.example: She hung a woodcut print above the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她在书桌上方挂了一幅木刻版画。
senses.why: Because the method repeats an image from a prepared surface, the noun names the picture that comes off the plate rather than the plate itself.
senses.whyCN: 由于这种方法是用准备好的版面反复复制图像，名词指的是从版上揭下来的那张画，而不是版本身。

senses.title: A mark left by pressure
senses.definition: a mark pressed into a surface by something touching it, such as a fingerprint or a footprint
senses.definitionCN: 某物接触表面时压出的痕迹，如指纹或脚印
senses.example: The police found a clear print on the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在玻璃上找到一枚清晰的指纹。
senses.why: Long before paper printing, the word meant the impression left by a stamp, and that older sense survives in fingerprints and footprints.
senses.whyCN: 在纸张印刷出现之前很久，这个词就指图章压出的痕迹，这个更早的意思活到了指纹、脚印这类说法里。

senses.title: To publish or carry in a paper
senses.definition: to include a piece of writing in a newspaper, magazine or book so that the public can read it
senses.definitionCN: 把一篇文字收进报纸、杂志或书里，让公众读到
senses.example: The paper decided to print her letter on the front page.
senses.exampleCN: 报社决定把她的来信登在头版。
senses.why: Publishing in the age of the press meant physically printing the text, so the machine's action became the word for making writing public.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷时代，发表文字就等于把文字真正印出来，于是机器的动作变成了「让文字公开」的说法。

intro.en: Print came into English as a noun for a pressed mark, from a French word for pressing, and only later grew the senses of printing text and pictures.
intro.cn: print 最初以名词身份进入英语，指压出来的痕迹，来自法语中表示「压」的词，后来才长出印文字、印图画的义项。

items.en: Premere meant to press or squeeze, and its participle pressus left marks on several European words.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤」，它的分词 pressus 在多种欧洲语言里留下了痕迹。

items.en: Old French preindre, to press, formed the feminine past participle preinte, a thing pressed or stamped.
items.cn: 古法语动词 preindre 意为「压」，其阴性过去分词 preinte 指被压出、被盖上印记的东西。

items.en: The noun preinte named the impression itself, the mark that a seal or a block leaves behind.
items.cn: 名词 preinte 指印记本身，即印章或印版留下的那道痕迹。

items.en: Middle English took the word as print or prent, meaning a mark or stamp, and by the fifteenth century also a printed book.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词写作 print 或 prent，指印记或图章，到十五世纪也指印出来的书。

items.en: With the printing press the verb spread to text and pictures, and in the computer age it was extended to paper output from a screen.
items.cn: 随着印刷机的普及，动词用法扩展到文字与图画；到了电脑时代，又扩展到屏幕上输出到纸面的行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on print and its verb stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for making text or images public.
note.cn: 形近组收由 print 及其动词词干构成的词；近义组收表示让文字或图像公之于众的动词。

entries.definition: A person whose trade is printing, or a machine that prints.
entries.definitionCN: 以印刷为业的人，或能打印的机器。

entries.definition: The act or trade of producing text and pictures with a press.
entries.definitionCN: 用印版制作文字与图画的行为或行业；印刷术。

entries.definition: Suitable or safe to be printed and shown to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 适合印出公开的；可以刊印的。

entries.definition: To press a mark into a surface, or the mark so made.
entries.definitionCN: 把痕迹压进表面，或这样留下的痕迹。

entries.definition: To make a piece of writing available to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 让一篇文字面向公众发行。

entries.definition: To make a version of something that matches the original.
entries.definitionCN: 做出与原物一致的复制品。

entries.definition: To press a design onto a surface with a tool.
entries.definitionCN: 用工具把图案压到表面上。

entries.definition: To make a copy of an image or text.
entries.definitionCN: 复制图像或文字。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the mark left by pressure and then moved to the machine that presses ink onto paper, so every sense is about transfer.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初指压力留下的痕迹，后来转指把油墨压到纸上的机器，所以每个义项讲的都是「转移」。

normal.en: Print comes from a verb for pressing, so the word still remembers the weight of a plate on paper.
normal.cn: print 出自表示「压」的动词，所以这个词至今记得印版压在纸上的分量。

normal.en: A printer is the thing that presses, and also the person whose trade was pressing.
normal.cn: printer 既是压印的机器，也是以压印为业的人。

normal.en: In print means the text has been pressed and is now public; out of print means the plates are no longer run.
normal.cn: in print 指文字已经印出、公开流传；out of print 指版子不再开印。

normal.en: Fine print is the small type at the bottom of a page, the part most people skip.
normal.cn: fine print 是页面底部的小字，多数人会跳过去不读。

normal.en: A fingerprint is literally a print made by a finger, the oldest sense still in daily use.
normal.cn: fingerprint 字面就是手指压出的印子，这是至今仍在日常使用的最古老义项。

abstract.en: Every sense of print is a transfer: ink to paper, screen to page, finger to glass.
abstract.cn: print 的每个义项都是一次转移：油墨到纸上，屏幕到纸面，手指到玻璃。

abstract.en: The word treats an image and a text alike, because both are pressed from one surface onto another.
abstract.cn: 这个词把图像和文字一视同仁，因为两者都是从一面压到另一面。

abstract.en: When a newspaper prints a letter, the physical act and the public act share one verb.
abstract.cn: 当报社 print 一封来信时，物理动作与公开行为共用一个动词。

examples.en: They print the school newspaper every Friday.
examples.cn: 他们每周五印校报。

examples.en: He printed the tickets and put them in an envelope.
examples.cn: 他把票打印出来放进信封。

examples.en: Her first novel is still in print after thirty years.
examples.cn: 她的第一部小说三十年后仍在印行。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a mark made by pressure; from that the senses run to ink on paper, computer output, pictures from a plate, fingerprints and published text.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是压力留下的痕迹；义项由此通向纸上的油墨、电脑输出、版上揭下的画、指纹，以及公开的文字。

intro.en: A Latin verb for pressing, its French descendants, and English endings that name the worker, the machine and the trade.

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb premere, to press, has the participle pressus, which also lies behind the English word press.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 premere 意为「压」，其分词 pressus 也正是英语 press 的来源。

definition_zh: 打印机；印刷工；印刷厂；照片冲印师
definition_en: a machine that prints text or pictures onto paper; a person who sets type and runs a press; a firm that produces printed matter; also a person who makes photographic prints
core_image: 纸从机器里一寸寸滑出来，字迹还带着墨的温热
scene: 深夜的办公室里只剩一盏台灯，最后一叠白纸被塞进机器，指示灯一闪一闪。The printer hummed for a moment and pushed out the last page of the report.
sceneCN: 这里 printer 指「打印机」（第 1 个义项：把文字和图像印到纸上的机器）；句意为打印机嗡响片刻，吐出了报告的最后一项内容。图中可辨识物件：台灯、白纸、闪着的指示灯。

pos.zh: 打印机；印刷工；印刷厂；照片冲印师

derivatives.zh: 由动词 print 加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「印刷；印刷业」，与 printer 同族
由 print 与 out 复合而成，义为「打印出来的文件；打印稿」
由 print 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可印刷的；适合印出来的」

senses.title: A machine that prints text or images onto paper
senses.definition: a machine, usually connected to a computer, that puts text or pictures onto paper
senses.definitionCN: 通常与计算机相连、把文字或图像印到纸上的机器
senses.example: The printer ran out of paper halfway through the chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 印到这一章一半时，打印机没纸了。
senses.why: The ending -er marks the one that performs an action, and English has long let that ending cover tools as well as people, so the box that does the printing takes over the name of the hand that once did it.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -er 标记「执行动作的那一个」，而英语早就允许它同时指工具和人，所以这台替人完成印刷的盒子沿用了从前那只手的名字。

senses.title: A person whose trade is setting type and running a press
senses.definition: a worker who arranges type and operates a printing press
senses.definitionCN: 负责排字并操作印刷机的工人
senses.example: Her grandfather was a printer who could read type upside down.
senses.exampleCN: 她祖父是印刷工，能倒着读字模。
senses.why: Before machines, printing was work of the hands: one man set the letters, another pulled the bar, and whoever owned that skill was simply called the printer.
senses.whyCN: 在有机器之前，印刷全靠一双手：有人拣字，有人扳动杠杆，掌握这门手艺的人就被称作印刷工，这是最老的一层意思。

senses.title: A firm that produces printed matter
senses.definition: a business that prints books, newspapers or other material for clients
senses.definitionCN: 替客户印书、印报或印其他材料的商号
senses.example: The book was sent to a printer in the next town.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书被送到邻镇的印刷厂。
senses.why: Once the trade gathered into workshops with several presses, the same word moved from the craftsman to the business he ran, because a customer dealt with the shop and not with one pair of hands.
senses.whyCN: 当这门手艺聚成拥有几台印刷机的作坊，同一个词就从手艺人转到他经营的商号，因为客户打交道的是那家店，而不是某一双手。

senses.title: A person who makes photographic prints
senses.definition: a person who produces final photographic prints from negatives or digital files
senses.definitionCN: 把底片或数字文件做成最终照片的人
senses.example: The printer adjusted the exposure before making the final copy.
senses.exampleCN: 冲印师在出最终成片前调整了曝光。
senses.why: Photography borrowed the word because a photographic print is also an image pressed onto treated paper, so whoever makes the final copy inherited the old title.
senses.whyCN: 摄影借用了这个词，因为照片同样是把影像压到处理过的纸上，于是负责做出最终成片的人继承了旧称呼。

intro.en: Printer is print plus an old agent ending, and print itself is usually traced through French to a Latin verb meaning to press, so the word starts from pressure rather than from ink.
intro.cn: printer 是 print 加一个古老的表人词尾；print 一般认为经法语上溯到表示「压」的拉丁语动词，所以这个词的起点是压力，而不是墨水。

items.en: The Latin verb premere meant to press, squeeze or push down, and its participle pressus stands behind the whole family of press words.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 premere 意为压、挤、按下，它的分词 pressus 支撑起 press 一族词。

items.en: Adding the prefix in- to premere produced imprimere, to press something into a surface, which is the picture behind every kind of printing.
items.cn: 在 premere 前加前缀 in- 得到 imprimere，意为把某物压进一个表面，这正是各种印刷背后的画面。

items.en: Old French used the noun preinte for an impression or a mark, and the verb preindre for making one; English took the noun first.
items.cn: 古法语用名词 preinte 指印痕、印记，动词 preindre 指压出印记；英语先借的是名词。

items.en: Middle English printen first meant to make a mark by pressure, and only later narrowed to pressing inked type onto paper.
items.cn: 中古英语 printen 最初指用压力留下痕迹，后来才缩小为把沾墨的字模压到纸上。

items.en: The agent ending -er first named the man at the press, and from the nineteenth century the same word was stretched to the machines that do the pressing for him.
items.cn: 表人的词尾 -er 先指站在印刷机旁的人；从十九世纪起，同一个词又被扩展到替他完成压印的机器上。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the print family and the Latin pressing stem; the near-meaning group gathers the other machines and trades that put marks on paper.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 print 词族与拉丁语表示「压」的词干展开；近义组收其他在纸上留下痕迹的机器与行当。

entries.definition: To press inked type or an image onto paper; the verb that printer is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 把沾墨的字模或图像压到纸上；printer 正是由这个动词构成。

entries.definition: The act or trade of producing printed matter.
entries.definitionCN: 生产印刷品的活动或行业。

entries.definition: A page or set of pages produced by a computer printer.
entries.definitionCN: 由计算机打印出来的纸页。

entries.definition: A mark pressed into a surface, or to press such a mark.
entries.definitionCN: 压进表面的印记，或压出这样的印记。

entries.definition: A machine that presses inked type onto paper, especially in a printing house.
entries.definitionCN: 把沾墨字模压到纸上的机器，尤指印刷厂的印刷机。

entries.definition: A machine that makes paper copies of documents.
entries.definitionCN: 把文件复制到纸上的机器。

entries.definition: A machine with keys that strike type onto paper.
entries.definitionCN: 用按键把字模打到纸上的机器。

entries.definition: A device that turns a printed page into a digital image, the opposite direction from a printer.
entries.definitionCN: 把纸页变成数字图像的设备，方向与打印机相反。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old agent ending laid on a verb that came from Latin pressing, so its reminders keep returning to pressure and to the hand that used to supply it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古老表人词尾加在一个源自拉丁语「压」的动词上，所以记忆线索总是回到压力和从前提供压力的那只手。

normal.en: Print comes from a Latin verb for pressing, so printing began as pressing rather than as writing.
normal.cn: print 出自拉丁语表示「压」的动词，所以印刷最初是压，而不是写。

normal.en: The -er in printer marks the one that does the action, the same ending as in teacher and builder.
normal.cn: printer 里的 -er 标记执行动作的那一个，和 teacher、builder 用的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: The machine sense is that same ending stretched to a tool, the way a computer is called a server.
normal.cn: 机器义只是把同一个词尾伸到工具身上，就像计算机被叫作 server 一样。

normal.en: Old French preinte gave English the noun print, and the t at the end is the trace of that borrowed participle.
normal.cn: 古法语 preinte 给英语送来了名词 print，词尾的 t 就是那个借来的分词留下的痕迹。

normal.en: Imprint keeps the Latin prefix in-: to press a mark into something.
normal.cn: imprint 保留了拉丁语前缀 in-，意思是把印记压进去。

abstract.en: A printer is a hand that became a box: the same job, the same pressure, only faster.
abstract.cn: 打印机是一只变成盒子的手：同样的活，同样的压力，只是更快。

abstract.en: Every printed page records two surfaces being pushed together, which is why the word belongs to the body before it belongs to the office.
abstract.cn: 每一页印刷品都记录着两个表面互相挤压，所以这个词先属于身体，后来才属于办公室。

abstract.en: When a word for a person turns into a word for a machine, a trade has been rebuilt around its tool.
abstract.cn: 当一个指人的词变成指机器的词，说明一门手艺已经围绕它的工具被重新搭建。

examples.en: The printer ran out of paper halfway through the chapter.
examples.cn: 印到这一章一半时，打印机没纸了。

examples.en: Her grandfather was a printer who could read type upside down.
examples.cn: 她祖父是印刷工，能倒着读字模。

examples.en: The book was sent to a printer in the next town.
examples.cn: 这本书被送到邻镇的印刷厂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普林特」——噗的一声，纸从机器里滑出来，那就是 printer。

root: print（印刷）加表人后缀 -er；print 经中古英语 printen、古法语 preinte 上溯到拉丁语 premere（压），加前缀 in- 的 imprimere 意为压印。

sensesIntro.en: The core is pressure transferring a mark; the senses divide into the machine that presses, the worker who once pressed, the firm that owns the presses, and the photographer who presses an image onto paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是压力把痕迹转移过去；义项由此分出压印的机器、从前动手的工人、拥有印刷机的商号，以及把影像压到纸上的冲印师。

core.cn: 核心意象：纸从机器里滑出来，还带着油墨的温热。

branches.cn: 纸页从嗡响的机器里滑出

branches.cn: 沾满油墨的手抬起字版

branches.cn: 院子里摆着印刷机的作坊

branches.cn: 暗房盘里浮着湿漉漉的影像

branches.cn: 同一种压力，一次压在纸上，一次压在胶片上

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of pressing, its prefixed form, the French noun of an impression, the English verb, and the endings that name the doer and the trade.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示压的拉丁语动词、加前缀的形式、法语中表示印记的名词、英语动词，以及命名做者与行当的词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere and its prefixed form imprimere stand at the head of this family, so the pressing image is recorded in Latin even though the modern trade word was shaped in French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 premere 及加前缀的 imprimere 处在这个词族的顶端，所以「压」的意象在拉丁语里就有记录，尽管现代行业词是在法语和英语里定型的。

definition_zh: 监狱；监禁；羁押场所；牢笼
definition_en: a building where convicted people are kept as punishment; the state of being kept there; a place of legal custody; and, figuratively, any situation a person cannot escape
core_image: 一扇高窗把光切成窄条，落在铁栏后面的石地上
scene: 雨夜里，高墙顶端只亮着一盏灯，铁门在身后合上，声音沉得像石头落进水里。He spent many years in a prison built on the edge of the moor.
sceneCN: 这里 prison 指「监狱」（第 1 个义项：关押已判刑者的建筑）；句意为他在荒原边上的一座监狱里度过了许多年。图中可辨识物件：高墙、灯、合上的铁门。

pos.zh: 监狱；监禁；羁押场所；牢笼

derivatives.zh: 由 prison 加表人后缀 -er 构成，义为「囚犯；俘虏」
由 prison 加表示「使进入」的前缀 im- 构成，义为「监禁；关押」
由 imprison 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「监禁；关押」

senses.title: A building where convicted people are kept
senses.definition: a building, usually with cells and high walls, where people are kept as punishment for crimes
senses.definitionCN: 通常设有牢房和高墙、用来关押罪犯以示惩罚的建筑
senses.example: The old prison is now a museum of penal history.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧监狱如今是刑罚史博物馆。
senses.why: The French noun named both the fact of captivity and the place of it, and the place is the sense that ordinary speech keeps at the front.
senses.whyCN: 这个法语名词既指被囚禁这件事，也指囚禁的地方；日常语言放在最前面的，是地方这一层。

senses.title: The state of being kept in such a place
senses.definition: the condition of being locked away as a legal punishment, used especially after the preposition in and without an article
senses.definitionCN: 作为法律惩罚被关起来的状态，尤用于介词 in 之后且不带冠词
senses.example: She has been in prison for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 她已入狱三年。
senses.why: Because the same noun could name captivity itself, English can use it as a mass noun after in, where no article is needed and no particular building is meant.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词本身就能指被囚禁的状态，英语便可以让它在 in 之后当不可数名词用，既不需要冠词，也不指某一座具体的建筑。

senses.title: A place of legal custody for people awaiting trial
senses.definition: a place where the law holds people who have not yet been tried or sentenced
senses.definitionCN: 法律上关押尚未受审或尚未判刑者的地方
senses.example: In older records, the town prison held debtors and people awaiting trial.
senses.exampleCN: 在更早的记载里，镇上的羁押所关过欠债的人和候审的人。
senses.why: Legal Latin and French used one word for anyone held by the law, whether sentenced or waiting, and older records keep that wider use although modern systems split the buildings.
senses.whyCN: 法律拉丁语和法语用同一个词指任何被法律看管的人，无论已判未判；旧记载保留了这个更宽的用法，尽管现代制度把两类建筑分开了。

senses.title: A place or situation from which one cannot escape
senses.definition: any place, relationship or habit that traps a person the way a cell traps a prisoner
senses.definitionCN: 像牢房困住囚犯那样，把人困住的任何地方、关系或习惯
senses.example: His own fame had become a prison he could not leave.
senses.exampleCN: 他自己的名气成了一座他走不出去的牢笼。
senses.why: A walled place is easy to move onto anything that keeps a person in, so the word follows the feeling of being enclosed rather than the stone.
senses.whyCN: 一座有围墙的地方很容易被挪去指任何把人困住的东西，所以这个词跟着的是被围住的感觉，而不是石头。

intro.en: Prison comes from a Latin verb for seizing: the word first names the act of taking a person, then the holding, then the building where the holding happens.
intro.cn: prison 出自拉丁语中表示「抓」的动词：这个词先指把人拿住这个动作，再指看管，最后指看管发生的那座建筑。

items.en: The Latin verb prehendere meant to seize or take hold of, formed from the prefix pre- and a root for grasping.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 prehendere 意为抓住、拿住，由前缀 pre- 加一个表示抓握的词根构成。

items.en: Its noun prehensio named the act of seizing, and by extension the holding of a person in custody.
items.cn: 它的名词 prehensio 指拿获这个动作，引申为把人看管起来。

items.en: Spoken Latin shortened the form to prensio, and it is this shorter stem that passed into French.
items.cn: 口语拉丁语把词形缩成 prensio，进入法语的正是这个较短的词干。

items.en: Old French prison meant both captivity and the place of captivity, and English borrowed it after the Norman conquest.
items.cn: 古法语 prison 既指被囚禁，也指囚禁的地方；诺曼征服之后英语借入这个词。

items.en: Middle English prisoun settled into modern prison, keeping the building and the state, and later took on the figurative sense of any trap.
items.cn: 中古英语 prisoun 定型为现代 prison，同时保留建筑与状态两义，后来又添上「任何牢笼」的比喻义。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin seizing stem and the English words built on prison; the near-meaning group gathers the other names for places and states of confinement.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语表示抓取的词干与由 prison 构成的英语词展开；近义组收其他表示关押地点与关押状态的词。

entries.definition: To put someone in prison; formed with the prefix im-.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人关进监狱；由前缀 im- 构成。

entries.definition: The act or state of being kept in prison.
entries.definitionCN: 监禁的行为或状态。

entries.definition: A person kept in prison or held captive.
entries.definitionCN: 被关在监狱里或被俘获的人。

entries.definition: Able to grasp, as a monkey's tail does; built on the same Latin root for seizing.
entries.definitionCN: 能够抓握的，如猴子的尾巴；建立在同一个表示抓取的拉丁词根上。

entries.definition: A place for people held for short periods or awaiting trial; the lighter everyday word in many varieties.
entries.definitionCN: 关押短期服刑者或候审者的地方；在许多英语变体里是较轻的日常说法。

entries.definition: A small room in a prison in which one prisoner is kept.
entries.definitionCN: 监狱里关押一名囚犯的小房间。

entries.definition: The state of being kept inside a closed space.
entries.definitionCN: 被关在封闭空间里的状态。

entries.definition: A prison, especially in American English, for people serving long sentences.
entries.definitionCN: 尤用于美式英语，指关押长期服刑者的监狱。

normalIntro.en: Everything in this family goes back to a Latin verb for grabbing a person, so the reminders follow the movement from seizing to holding to the walls that keep the holding in place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词族的一切都回到拉丁语中「抓住一个人」的动词，所以记忆线索跟着从拿获、看管到砌起围墙这条路线走。

normal.en: Prehendere is Latin for seize, so a prison is where the people who have been seized are kept.
normal.cn: prehendere 是拉丁语的「抓住」，所以 prison 就是关住那些被抓住之人的地方。

normal.en: Old French used one word for both the place and the state, which is why English says in prison without an article.
normal.cn: 古法语用同一个词指地方和状态，所以英语说 in prison 时不加冠词。

normal.en: Imprison adds the prefix im-, the same in- that appears in enclose: to put someone inside.
normal.cn: imprison 加了前缀 im-，就是 enclose 里的那个 in-，意思是把人放进去。

normal.en: Prisoner adds -er, the old French ending for a person concerned with something.
normal.cn: prisoner 加了 -er，那是古法语里表示「与某事相关的人」的词尾。

normal.en: Jail and prison are near twins, but prison is the heavier word and usually names the place for long sentences.
normal.cn: jail 与 prison 像一对双胞胎，但 prison 分量更重，通常指关长期刑期的地方。

abstract.en: The word travels from a hand closing on an arm to a wall closing on a life.
abstract.cn: 这个词从一只抓住胳膊的手，走到一堵围住一生的墙。

abstract.en: Prison as a state needs no article, because captivity is treated as a condition rather than as a building.
abstract.cn: 作为状态的 prison 不带冠词，因为被囚禁被当成一种处境，而不是一座建筑。

abstract.en: Once a noun names a walled place, it can be moved onto any boundary that holds a person in.
abstract.cn: 一旦一个名词指过有围墙的地方，它就能被挪去指任何把人困住的界线。

examples.en: The old prison is now a museum of penal history.
examples.cn: 那座旧监狱如今是刑罚史博物馆。

examples.en: She has been in prison for three years.
examples.cn: 她已入狱三年。

examples.en: His own fame had become a prison he could not leave.
examples.cn: 他自己的名气成了一座他走不出去的牢笼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普里森」——人被关进石头墙里，只能听见自己的呼吸声。

root: 古法语 prison（囚禁、监牢）经中古英语 prisoun 进入现代英语；更早可上溯到拉丁语 prehensio（拿获），动词 prehendere（抓住）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person being seized and held; the senses divide into the building, the condition, the legal custody that precedes sentencing, and the figurative trap.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一个人被抓并被看住」；义项由此分出建筑、状态、判刑前的法律羁押，以及比喻的牢笼。

core.cn: 核心意象：高窗把光切成窄条，落在铁栏后的石地上。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of seizing, its noun of arrest, the French noun of captivity, the English borrowing, and the endings that build prisoner and imprisonment from it.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示抓取的拉丁语动词、表示逮捕的名词、法语中表示囚禁的名词、英语借词，以及由此构成 prisoner 与 imprisonment 的词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Prehendere and its noun prehensio are securely recorded in Latin, and the shortened prensio explains the French form that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: prehendere 及其名词 prehensio 在拉丁语里有明确记录，缩短的 prensio 则解释了英语所借的那个法语词形。

definition_zh: 囚犯；俘虏；被扣押者；受困于……的人
definition_en: a person kept in prison as a punishment; a person captured in war or held captive; a person held by a group; and anyone trapped by a situation they cannot leave
core_image: 铁栏后面抬起的一张脸，眼睛还盯着门外的一点光
scene: 探视室的玻璃上蒙着一层雾，穿灰色衣服的人把手掌贴在另一侧，隔着反光的表面与家人对视。The prisoner pressed one hand to the glass and tried to smile.
sceneCN: 这里 prisoner 指「囚犯」（第 1 个义项：在狱中服刑的人）；句意为那名囚犯把一只手贴在玻璃上，努力笑了一下。图中可辨识物件：探视玻璃、灰色衣服、贴在玻璃上的手掌。

pos.zh: 囚犯；俘虏；被扣押者；受困于……的人

derivatives.zh: 由 prison 加前缀 im- 构成，义为「监禁」，与 prisoner 同族
由 imprison 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「监禁；关押」
prisoner 的词干，义为「监狱；监禁」，加表人后缀后指被关在里面的人

senses.title: A person kept in a prison as punishment
senses.definition: a person who is kept in a prison while serving a sentence for a crime
senses.definitionCN: 因犯罪在狱中服刑、被关押的人
senses.example: The prisoner was allowed one hour of exercise a day.
senses.exampleCN: 那名囚犯每天获准活动一小时。
senses.why: The Old French ending -ier marked a person connected with something, so prisonier was simply the person who belonged to a prison.
senses.whyCN: 古法语词尾 -ier 标记「与某事物相关的人」，所以 prisonier 就是属于监狱的那个人。

senses.title: A person captured by an enemy in war
senses.definition: a soldier or civilian taken by an enemy force and held during a war
senses.definitionCN: 战争中被敌方捉住并扣押的军人或平民
senses.example: The soldiers were taken prisoner before they reached the river.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们还没到河边就被俘虏了。
senses.why: War produced captives long before modern prisons existed, and the same word covered them because both were people held against their will.
senses.whyCN: 早在现代监狱出现之前，战争就已经产生俘虏；同一个词能兼指两者，因为他们都是被违背意愿扣住的人。

senses.title: A person held captive by a group, often for bargaining
senses.definition: a person seized and held by a group, sometimes to force others to meet demands
senses.definitionCN: 被某一群体捉住扣留的人，有时用来迫使他人答应条件
senses.example: The prisoner was released after two weeks of negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 经过两周谈判，那名被扣押者获释了。
senses.why: Once the word means anyone held, it fits a hostage as well; what differs is who holds the power, not the word itself.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词泛指任何被扣住的人，它自然也能指人质；不同的只是谁握着权力，而不是词本身。

senses.title: A person trapped by a situation or habit
senses.definition: a person who cannot escape a condition, relationship or habit that limits them
senses.definitionCN: 无法摆脱某种限制自己的处境、关系或习惯的人
senses.example: He became a prisoner of his own routine and stopped travelling.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了自己日常习惯的囚徒，不再出门旅行。
senses.why: The literal cell becomes a metaphor: whatever a person cannot walk away from can be named as the thing that holds them prisoner.
senses.whyCN: 真实的牢房转成比喻：凡是人走不开的东西，都可以被说成把他困住的那个东西。

intro.en: Prisoner is the person-shaped member of the prison family: French put its ending for an involved person onto prison, and English borrowed the whole word rather than building it fresh.
intro.cn: prisoner 是 prison 词族里「人」的那一个：法语把表示「相关之人」的词尾加到 prison 上，英语整词借入，而不是自己新造。

items.en: Prehendere meant to seize, and its noun prehensio named the taking of a person into custody.
items.cn: prehendere 意为抓住，其名词 prehensio 指把人拿获、看管。

items.en: Old French prison named both captivity and the place where captives were kept.
items.cn: 古法语 prison 既指被囚禁，也指关押被囚者的地方。

items.en: Adding the ending -ier, which marked a person concerned with something, produced prisonier, the person held.
items.cn: 加上表示「与某事相关的人」的词尾 -ier，得到 prisonier，即被关押的那个人。

items.en: English borrowed the form as prisoner and used it for captives in war as well as for people in gaols.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 prisoner，既指狱中的人，也指战场上的俘虏。

items.en: Modern English keeps the word for legal inmates and extends it to hostages and to anyone trapped by circumstances.
items.cn: 现代英语保留它指法律意义上的在押者，并扩展到人质以及任何被处境困住的人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the prison stem and its Latin source; the near-meaning group gathers the other English names for people who are held.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 prison 词干及其拉丁语来源展开；近义组收英语里其他指「被扣住的人」的名称。

entries.definition: The place or state that gives prisoner its stem.
entries.definitionCN: 给出 prisoner 词干的地点或状态。

entries.definition: To put someone into prison; formed with the prefix im-.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人关进监狱；由前缀 im- 构成。

entries.definition: The act or state of being imprisoned.
entries.definitionCN: 监禁的行为或状态。

entries.definition: Able to grasp; from the same Latin root for seizing that stands behind prison.
entries.definitionCN: 能够抓握的；出自 prison 背后那个表示抓取的拉丁词根。

entries.definition: A person held by an enemy or a captor.
entries.definitionCN: 被敌人或捕获者扣住的人。

entries.definition: A person living in a prison or another institution.
entries.definitionCN: 住在监狱或其他机构里的人。

entries.definition: A person found guilty of a crime and serving a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 被判定有罪并在服刑的人。

entries.definition: A person kept in official custody, often without a criminal sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 被官方羁押的人，常常并未被判刑。

normalIntro.en: This is a place word with a person ending on it, so the useful reminders keep the stem and the ending separate and then let them travel into war and metaphor.
normalIntro.cn: 这是一个地点词加表人词尾构成的词，所以有用的记忆法是先把词干和词尾分开，再看它怎样走进战场和比喻。

normal.en: Prisoner is prison plus the old French ending -ier, which names a person connected with a place or thing.
normal.cn: prisoner 是 prison 加古法语词尾 -ier，那个词尾命名与某地或某物相关的人。

normal.en: The same ending appears in officer and grenadier, all of them people attached to something.
normal.cn: 同一个词尾也出现在 officer 和 grenadier 里，它们都指依附于某物的人。

normal.en: Prison supplies the stem: take away the ending and you have the place.
normal.cn: prison 提供词干：去掉词尾，剩下的就是那个地方。

normal.en: Take prisoner is a fixed phrase in which the verb means to capture, not to jail.
normal.cn: take prisoner 是固定说法，其中的动词是「俘获」，不是「关进监狱」。

normal.en: Prisoner of war keeps the old sense of a captive taken in battle, which predates the modern prison.
normal.cn: prisoner of war 保留了战场上被俘的旧义，那一层比现代监狱更早。

abstract.en: One word holds the man behind bars and the man on a battlefield, because both have lost the power to walk away.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装着铁栏后的人和战场上的人，因为两者都失去了走开的权力。

abstract.en: The ending is what makes it personal: the place stays a place until -ier turns it into someone.
abstract.cn: 词尾让它变成了人：地点本来只是地点，直到 -ier 把它变成某个人。

abstract.en: A prisoner of habit shows how easily a legal word becomes a picture of the mind.
abstract.cn: 「习惯的囚徒」说明一个法律词多么容易变成一幅心理画面。

examples.en: The prisoner pressed one hand to the glass and tried to smile.
examples.cn: 那名囚犯把一只手贴在玻璃上，努力笑了一下。

examples.en: The soldiers were taken prisoner before they reached the river.
examples.cn: 士兵们还没到河边就被俘虏了。

examples.en: He became a prisoner of his own routine and stopped travelling.
examples.cn: 他成了自己日常习惯的囚徒，不再出门旅行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普里兹纳」——被关在里面的人，只能数着窗格上的影子。

root: prison（监狱）加表人后缀 -er（来自古法语 -ier，源自拉丁语 -arius）；prison 经古法语上溯到拉丁语 prehensio（拿获）、prehendere（抓住）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person held by force; the senses divide by who holds them: the court, the enemy, an armed group, and finally a condition of the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一个被强力扣住的人」；义项按扣押者分开：法庭、敌人、武装团伙，最后是心里的某种处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face lifted behind iron bars, eyes fixed on a patch of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁栏后抬起的一张脸，眼睛盯着外面的一点光。

branches.en: a hand flat against visiting-room glass
branches.cn: 贴在探视室玻璃上的手掌

branches.en: a column of captured men on a road
branches.cn: 路上被押走的一队人

branches.en: a locked room and a negotiator outside
branches.cn: 锁着的房间与门外的谈判者

branches.en: a man who never leaves his own street
branches.cn: 从不走出自己那条街的人

branches.en: the same word for the jailed and the captured
branches.cn: 被关的与被俘的共用同一个词

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of seizing, its noun of arrest, the French place word, the French person ending, and the English noun that grew from them.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示抓取的拉丁语动词、表示逮捕的名词、法语的地点词、法语的表人词尾，以及由它们长出的英语名词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb of seizing and its noun of arrest are recorded, and the French person ending -ier is itself a descendant of Latin -arius, so the whole word is Latin in its bones.
latinIntro.cn: 表示抓取的拉丁语动词与表示逮捕的名词都有记录，法语的表人词尾 -ier 本身也是拉丁语 -arius 的后代，所以这个词骨子里是拉丁语。

definition_zh: 私人的；私有的；私密的；私立的；僻静的；列兵
definition_en: belonging to one person or a small group rather than to the public; kept secret from others; not run by the state; free from other people; and, as a noun, a soldier of the lowest rank
core_image: 一扇关着的门后面，桌上摊着只给自己看的信
scene: 周末午后，小咖啡馆最里面的角落摆着一张矮桌，说话的人把声音压低，不希望邻座听见。They chose a private corner of the coffee shop to discuss the contract.
sceneCN: 这里 private 指「私密的、不让旁人听见的」（第 2 个义项：只让少数人知道或参与的）；句意为他们挑了咖啡馆里一个私密的角落谈合同。图中可辨识物件：矮桌、压低声音的两个人、邻座的空椅。

pos.zh: 私人的；私有的；私密的；私立的；僻静的
列兵；二等兵

derivatives.zh: 由 private 加名词后缀 -acy 构成，义为「隐私；私密」
由 private 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「私下地；以私人身份」
与 private 同源，出自拉丁语 privatio，义为「匮乏；剥夺」

senses.title: Belonging to one person rather than to the public
senses.definition: owned by or intended for one person or a small group, not for everyone
senses.definitionCN: 属于或专供一个人、一小群人，而不是给所有人的
senses.example: The letters are part of his private collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件是他私人收藏的一部分。
senses.why: Latin privus meant single or individual, the direct opposite of publicus, so the first sense is ownership narrowed down to one person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 privus 意为单个的、个人的，正好与 publicus 相对；所以第一层意思就是把归属缩到一个人身上。

senses.title: Kept from the knowledge of others
senses.definition: shared with only a few people and deliberately kept away from the public
senses.definitionCN: 只在少数人之间分享、有意不让公众知道的
senses.example: The meeting was private, so no notes were published.
senses.exampleCN: 那场会是不公开的，所以没有公布记录。
senses.why: What belongs to one person is also what only that person may know, so the ownership sense slides naturally into secrecy.
senses.whyCN: 属于一个人的东西，也就是只许那个人知道的东西，于是「归属」这一层自然而然地滑向「保密」。

senses.title: Not run or paid for by the state
senses.definition: owned and managed by an individual or a company rather than by the government
senses.definitionCN: 由个人或公司拥有经营，而不是由政府办的
senses.example: She moved her son from a state school to a private one.
senses.exampleCN: 她把儿子从公立学校转到了私立学校。
senses.why: When the state became the default provider of schools and hospitals, anything outside it was marked with the old word for what belongs to an individual, and this institutional sense followed.
senses.whyCN: 当国家成为学校和医院的默认提供者，凡是国家之外的就用那个表示「属于个人」的旧词来标记，这一层机构义便随之出现。

senses.title: Quiet and free from other people
senses.definition: away from crowds and public view, so that a person is not observed
senses.definitionCN: 远离人群和公众视线，人不被旁人看到
senses.example: The garden is private, and no visitors are allowed inside.
senses.exampleCN: 那座花园是私家的，访客不得入内。
senses.why: A place can be private too: if it belongs to one household, outsiders stay out, and the result is the quiet of a spot no one else enters.
senses.whyCN: 地方也可以是 private：它属于一户人家，外人就不进来，结果就是一处没人进入的安静之地。

senses.title: A soldier of the lowest rank
senses.definition: a soldier of the lowest rank, especially in the British army
senses.definitionCN: 最低军衔的士兵，尤指英国陆军中的
senses.example: He joined up as a private and retired as a sergeant.
senses.exampleCN: 他入伍时是列兵，退役时已是中士。
senses.why: The noun began as private soldier, a man serving in his own private capacity rather than as an officer, and the shorter form kept only the rank.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词起初写作 private soldier，指以个人身份服役、而非军官的人；后来缩写只留下了军衔这一层。

intro.en: Private comes from a Latin adjective meaning single or set apart, and its family keeps two faces: what belongs to one person, and what has been cut off from the rest.
intro.cn: private 出自一个意为「单个的、被分出来的」拉丁语形容词，它的词族始终保留两张面孔：属于一个人的，以及从其余部分中割出来的。

items.en: Privus meant single, individual or set apart, and it stood opposite publicus, what belongs to the people as a whole.
items.cn: privus 意为单个的、个人的、被单独分出来的，与表示「属于全体人民的」publicus 相对。

items.en: The verb privare meant to set apart or to deprive, and it supplied the idea of taking something away from the group.
items.cn: 动词 privare 意为使分离、剥夺，给出「把某物从群体中拿走」这一层意思。

items.en: Its participle privatus described a person withdrawn from public office, and from that came the sense of personal rather than official.
items.cn: 它的分词 privatus 形容退离公职的人，由此生出「属于个人而非公职」的意思。

items.en: Old French privat meant private, intimate and secret, and Middle English borrowed the word with that whole spread of meaning.
items.cn: 古法语 privat 意为私人的、亲近的、秘密的，中古英语把这一整片含义一起借了过来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective for ownership, secrecy, non-state services and quiet places, while private soldier was shortened to private for the lowest rank.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词的四种用法：归属、保密、非国营与僻静；private soldier 则缩成 private，指最低军衔。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem priv- and the words English built on it; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives about what belongs to one person or is kept hidden.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁词干 priv- 及英语在它上面造出的词展开；近义组收表示「属于一个人」或「被藏起来」的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being free from public attention; built on the same stem with -acy.
entries.definitionCN: 不受公众注意的状态；同一词干加 -acy 构成。

entries.definition: In a private way, not publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 以私下的方式，非公开地。

entries.definition: The state of lacking something necessary; from Latin privatio.
entries.definitionCN: 缺少必需之物的状态；来自拉丁语 privatio。

entries.definition: To take something away from someone; built on the same Latin verb privare.
entries.definitionCN: 从某人那里拿走某物；建立在同一个拉丁动词 privare 上。

entries.definition: Relating to one particular person rather than to others.
entries.definitionCN: 与某一个特定的人有关，而非与其他人有关。

entries.definition: Kept hidden from other people.
entries.definitionCN: 对其他的人隐藏起来的。

entries.definition: Meant to be kept private between a few people.
entries.definitionCN: 只应在少数人之间保密的。

entries.definition: Single and separate, belonging to one person.
entries.definitionCN: 单个而分开的，属于一个人的。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin adjective for what is single and cut off from the group, and every branch of meaning keeps either the belonging or the cutting.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在一个拉丁语形容词上，本义是「单个的、从群体里分出来的」，它的每一支意思都保留着「归属」或「切割」其中之一。

normal.en: Privus is Latin for single or individual, and it stands opposite publicus, the source of public.
normal.cn: privus 是拉丁语的「单个的、个人的」，与 publicus 相对，而 public 正出自后者。

normal.en: Privare means to set apart or deprive, which is why private and deprive share a stem.
normal.cn: privare 意为使分离、剥夺，所以 private 与 deprive 共用一个词干。

normal.en: Privacy adds -acy, the ending that turns an adjective into a state, as in accuracy.
normal.cn: privacy 加了 -acy，这个词尾把形容词变成状态，和 accuracy 一样。

normal.en: Private soldier was shortened to private, so the noun keeps only the rank, not the man.
normal.cn: private soldier 缩成了 private，于是这个名词只留下军衔，不再指那个人。

normal.en: In private is a fixed phrase: the preposition turns the adjective into an adverbial of manner.
normal.cn: in private 是固定说法，介词把这个形容词变成了方式状语。

abstract.en: The word carries both a belonging and a wall: something is mine because it is kept away from you.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时带着归属和一道墙：某物之所以是我的，正因为它被挡在你之外。

abstract.en: Public and private are the same coin struck twice, one face for the many and one for the one.
abstract.cn: public 与 private 是同一枚硬币的两面，一面给众人，一面给个人。

abstract.en: A private soldier is private in the oldest sense: a man serving as himself, not as an officer.
abstract.cn: 列兵的 private 用的是最老的那层意思：以本人身份服役，而不是以军官身份。

examples.en: The letters are part of his private collection.
examples.cn: 这些信件是他私人收藏的一部分。

examples.en: She moved her son from a state school to a private one.
examples.cn: 她把儿子从公立学校转到了私立学校。

examples.en: He joined up as a private and retired as a sergeant.
examples.cn: 他入伍时是列兵，退役时已是中士。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普莱维特」——「不来往」的那扇门后面，才是 private 的地方。

root: 拉丁语 privus（个人的、单独的）→ privare（使分离、剥夺）→ privatus（退离公职的、私人的）→ 古法语 privat → 中古英语 privat → private。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to one person and is therefore cut off from the rest; the senses divide into ownership, secrecy, non-state service, quiet space, and the private soldier.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「属于一个人、因而与其余部分隔开」；义项由此分出归属、保密、非国营、安静的空间，以及列兵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed door with a letter on the table behind it, written for one reader only.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇关着的门，门后桌上摊着一封只给一个人看的信。

branches.en: a drawer of letters with one name on it
branches.cn: 只写着一个名字的抽屉

branches.en: a door closed before a quiet conversation
branches.cn: 悄悄谈话前关上的门

branches.en: a school with its own gate and its own fees
branches.cn: 自带大门与学费的学校

branches.en: a walled garden nobody else enters
branches.cn: 别人不得进入的围墙花园

branches.en: a young soldier standing at the end of the line
branches.cn: 队列末尾站着的年轻士兵

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective for what is single and set apart, its verb of depriving, the French form, and the English endings that name the state and the manner.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「单个、被分出」的拉丁语形容词、表示剥夺的动词、法语词形，以及命名状态与方式的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin privus and privare are the secure base of this family, and privatus shows how an adjective of being set apart became the ordinary word for personal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 privus 与 privare 是这个词族可靠的根基，privatus 则展示了一个「被分开」的形容词如何变成表示「私人」的日常词。

definition_zh: 奖品；奖赏；可贵之物；珍视；获奖的
definition_en: something given to the winner of a contest; something valuable that is worth striving for; to value something highly; and, before a noun, award-winning or of outstanding quality
core_image: 人群中高高举起的一只银杯
scene: 礼堂里坐满了人，主持人念出名字的一刻，后排的女孩愣了一下才站起来。The girl walked to the front to collect her prize while the whole hall clapped.
sceneCN: 这里的 prize 是「奖品」（第 1 个义项：比赛或评比中发给获胜者的东西）；句意为全场鼓掌时，女孩走到台前领取奖品。图中可辨识物件：礼堂座位、领奖台、银杯。

pos.zh: 奖品；奖赏；可贵之物
珍视；重视
获奖的；一流的

derivatives.zh: 由 prize（奖）与 fighter（打斗者）复合而成，义为「职业拳击手」
由 prize 与 winner 复合而成，义为「获奖者」

senses.title: Something given to the winner of a contest
senses.definition: an object, title, or sum of money given to the person who wins a competition or does something outstanding
senses.definitionCN: 发给比赛获胜者或表现突出者的物品、称号或奖金
senses.example: The first prize was a small silver cup.
senses.exampleCN: 一等奖是一只小银杯。
senses.why: The French source carried two meanings at once, cost and reward; English kept the reward half for what a winner carries away.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源同时带着代价与回报两层；英语把回报那一半留下来，用来指获胜者带走的东西。

senses.title: Something valuable that is worth striving for
senses.titleCN: 可贵之物；值得争取的目标
senses.definition: a thing or quality so valuable that people work hard to obtain or keep it
senses.definitionCN: 珍贵到人们愿意努力去获得或守住的东西或品质
senses.example: A quiet hour in the morning is the real prize of an early start.
senses.exampleCN: 早晨安静的一小时，才是早起真正的收获。
senses.why: Once a prize is what you get for effort, the word can name anything worth that effort, even something nobody can hand you.
senses.whyCN: 既然 prize 是努力之后得到的东西，这个词就能指任何值得那份努力的事物，哪怕没有人能把它递到你手上。

senses.title: To value something highly
senses.definition: to think that something is extremely valuable and to treat it with care
senses.definitionCN: 认为某物极为宝贵，因而小心对待
senses.example: She prizes the letters her grandmother wrote more than any jewellery.
senses.exampleCN: 比起任何首饰，她更珍视祖母写的那些信。
senses.why: The same French verb meant to set a price on and to esteem; English turned the second half into a verb of holding something dear.
senses.whyCN: 同一个法语动词既表示给某物定价，也表示看重；英语取了后一半，变成把某物看得珍贵的动词。

senses.title: Award-winning or of outstanding quality
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe something that has won an award or is judged excellent
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，形容获得过奖项或被认为极为出色的东西
senses.example: The shop window was filled with prize vegetables from the village show.
senses.exampleCN: 橱窗里摆满了村里评比中获奖的蔬菜。
senses.why: Because a prize marks the best of a class, the noun moved in front of other nouns and became an adjective meaning top-grade.
senses.whyCN: 因为奖标记的是一类中最好的，这个名词就移到别的名词前面，变成表示头等的形容词。

intro.en: Prize and price are twins: both descend from Latin pretium, the word for worth, and only later did English split cost from reward.
intro.cn: prize 与 price 是一对双生词：两者都出自拉丁语 pretium（价值），英语后来才把代价与回报分开。

items.en: Pretium meant price, value, or worth, the amount at which a thing was valued, whether in coins or in esteem.
items.cn: pretium 意为价格、价值、所值，指一件东西被估出的分量，可以是用钱算的，也可以是用敬重算的。

items.en: Spoken Latin formed appretiare, to set a value on something, and this verb passed into French as the ordinary word for appraising.
items.cn: 口语拉丁语造出 appretiare，意为给某物估价，这个动词进入法语后成为平常说「评价」的词。

items.en: Old French pris meant both price and worth, and also the reward or honour given to a person who had done well.
items.cn: 古法语 pris 既指价格与价值，也指给表现优异者的回报或荣誉。

items.en: Middle English borrowed pris with both halves intact, so one word could speak of what a thing cost and of what a winner received.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 pris 时两半都还在，同一个词既能说一件东西值多少钱，也能说获胜者得到了什么。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the spellings settled apart: price kept cost, prize kept reward and the verb to value highly; the sense to force open belongs to a different word, Old French prise, a grasp.
items.cn: 十六世纪起两种拼写分家：price 守住代价，prize 守住回报以及珍视这个动词；而撬开一义属于另一个词，来自古法语 prise（抓住）。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the twin word and the shapes closest to it in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for awards and for things won.
note.cn: 形近组收那对双生词以及拼写最接近的几个词；近义组收表示奖项与所得之物的词。

entries.definition: The amount of money a thing costs; it split from the same Latin pretium as prize.
entries.definitionCN: 一件东西所需的钱数；与 prize 同出拉丁语 pretium，后来分家。

entries.definition: To force something open with a lever, the British spelling of the American pry; a different word from Old French prise.
entries.definitionCN: 用杠杆撬开，是美式 pry 的英式拼写；与 prize 来源不同。

entries.definition: To express approval or admiration; it also goes back to Latin pretium, but through a French verb meaning to value.
entries.definitionCN: 表达赞许或钦佩；它也上溯到拉丁语 pretium，走的是意为「看重」的法语动词。

entries.definition: A person who fights for money in the ring; a compound of prize and fighter.
entries.definitionCN: 在拳台上为奖金而战的人；由 prize 与 fighter 复合而成。

entries.definition: Something given formally to recognise merit or a win.
entries.definitionCN: 为表彰功绩或胜利而正式发给的东西。

entries.definition: Something given in return for effort or good behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 因付出努力或表现良好而得到的回报。

entries.definition: An object kept as a symbol of a victory.
entries.definitionCN: 作为胜利象征而被保存的物件。

entries.definition: A flat piece of metal given to a winner or a hero.
entries.definitionCN: 发给获胜者或英雄的金属片。

normalIntro.en: The word shares a Latin ancestor with price, and its family keeps both halves of that ancestor: what a thing is worth, and what a person is worth to you.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词与 price 共有一个拉丁祖先，它的同族保留了这个祖先的两半：一件东西值多少，以及一个人在你心里值多少。

normal.en: Pretium in Latin means worth, so prize began as a statement about value rather than about medals.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pretium 意为价值，所以 prize 最初讲的是值多少，而不是奖牌。

normal.en: Price and prize are the same Latin word arriving twice: one kept the cost, the other kept the reward.
normal.cn: price 与 prize 是同一个拉丁词抵达两次：一个留下代价，一个留下回报。

normal.en: The verb prize, as in prize something highly, keeps the old sense of setting a value on a thing.
normal.cn: 动词 prize（如 prize something highly）保留的正是给某物估个高价的老意思。

normal.en: Prize before a noun, as in prize bull, works like an adjective: the animal that took the award.
normal.cn: prize 放在名词前（如 prize bull）就像形容词：拿过奖的那头牲口。

normal.en: The -prise in surprise comes from another word meaning a grasp, and it only looks like prize.
normal.cn: surprise 里的 -prise 来自另一个意为「抓住」的词，只是长得像 prize。

abstract.en: A single Latin word for worth grew two English faces, one asking what you pay and one asking what you win.
abstract.cn: 一个表示价值的拉丁词长出两张英语面孔：一张问你付多少，一张问你赢什么。

abstract.en: A prize is worth made visible: a cup on a shelf turns an invisible judgement into an object you can hold.
abstract.cn: prize 是被看见的价值：架子上的一只杯子，把无形的评判变成可以拿在手里的东西。

abstract.en: To prize something is to put a price on it in the old sense, not to sell it but to admit it cannot be replaced.
abstract.cn: to prize 某物是用老意思给它标价，不是要卖掉它，而是承认它无可替代。

examples.en: The first prize was a small silver cup.
examples.cn: 一等奖是一只小银杯。

examples.en: She prizes the letters her grandmother wrote more than any jewellery.
examples.cn: 比起任何首饰，她更珍视祖母写的那些信。

examples.en: The girl walked to the front to collect her prize.
examples.cn: 女孩走到台前领取奖品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑来事」——好事扑过来，得了奖，就是 prize。

root: 拉丁语 pretium（价值、价格）→ 口语拉丁语 appretiare（估价）→ 古法语 pris（价格；回报）→ 中古英语 pris → 现代英语分化为 price（价格）与 prize（奖品）。撬开一义另出古法语 prise（抓住），与前一支无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is worth; the senses divide into the reward a winner takes, the valuable thing worth working for, the act of valuing, and the adjective for what has won.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是价值；义项分成获胜者拿走的回报、值得为之努力的可贵之物、珍视的动作，以及形容获奖之物的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silver cup lifted above a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群中高高举起的一只银杯。

branches.en: a cup raised at the front of a hall
branches.cn: 礼堂前方被举起的一只杯子

branches.en: a still morning hour that nobody can buy
branches.cn: 没人买得到的一段安静晨光

branches.en: a hand resting on an old bundle of letters
branches.cn: 一只手按在一叠旧信上

branches.en: ribbons on vegetables at a village show
branches.cn: 村里评比中系在蔬菜上的绶带

branches.en: the same judgement, given once as an object and once as a label
branches.cn: 同一种评判，一次给成物件，一次给成标签

intro.en: The word goes back to one Latin noun of value, a Latin verb of valuing, and the French forms that split into two English words; the eight entries keep that fork visible.
intro.cn: 这个词上溯到一个表示价值的拉丁名词、一个表示估价的拉丁动词，以及分成两个英语词的法语词形；下面八条让这个分岔看得见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun pretium and the verb built on it are directly recorded, which is why price, prize and praise can all be traced to one source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 pretium 以及由它构成的动词都有直接记录，所以 price、prize、praise 才能一同追到同一个源头。

items.meaning: a reward given to a winner

definition_zh: 很可能；大概；想必；多半
definition_en: used to say that something is very likely to be true or to happen, or to make a guess sound less certain
core_image: 云压得很低，出门前顺手拿起一把伞
scene: 窗外的云压得很低，风把晾着的衣服吹得直响，母亲在门口把伞塞进孩子书包。It will probably rain before the children get home.
sceneCN: 这里的 probably 表示「很可能」（第 1 个义项：对将要发生的事作出高概率判断）；句意为在孩子们到家之前多半会下雨。图中可辨识物件：压低的云、被风吹起的衣服、塞进书包的伞。

pos.zh: 很可能；大概；想必

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「很可能的；可信的」
由 probable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可能性；概率」
由否定前缀 im- 加 probable 构成，义为「不大可能的」

senses.title: Very likely to be true or to happen
senses.definition: used to say that something is more likely than not, though not certain
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事发生的可能性大于不发生的可能性，但并非确定
senses.example: The train will probably leave from platform three.
senses.exampleCN: 火车很可能会从三号站台开出。
senses.why: Latin probabilis described what could be proved or accepted, and the adverb keeps that measured confidence rather than absolute certainty.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 probabilis 形容能够被证明或接受的东西，副词保留的正是这种有分寸的把握，而不是绝对的确定。

senses.title: Judging from the evidence, almost certainly
senses.definition: used when the facts already known point strongly to one conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 在已知事实强烈指向某个结论时使用
senses.example: She has not answered for two days, so she is probably away.
senses.exampleCN: 她两天没回音，想必是不在。
senses.why: When the likelihood rests on evidence rather than on hope, the same adverb shifts from prediction to inference about what has already happened.
senses.whyCN: 当这种可能性建立在证据而不是愿望上，同一个副词就从预测将来转到推断已经发生的事。

senses.title: Used to soften a guess about other people
senses.definition: used politely to avoid sounding too sure about another person's situation or reasons
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地避免对别人的处境或理由显得过于肯定
senses.example: You probably have your own reasons for saying nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 你大概有自己的理由不开口。
senses.why: Saying probably hands part of the judgement back to the listener, which is why the word so often appears when a speaker wants to be tactful.
senses.whyCN: 说出 probably 等于把一部分判断交回给听者，所以说话人想留面子时，这个词特别常出现。

intro.en: Probably belongs to a Latin family of testing and proving: what is probable is what can stand up to examination.
intro.cn: probably 属于拉丁语中检验、证明这一族词：probable 就是经得起检验的东西。

items.en: Probus meant upright, honest, and sound, said of a person or a thing that could be trusted without further proof.
items.cn: probus 意为正直、诚实、可靠，用来形容不必再验证就可信任的人或物。

items.en: The verb probare meant to test, to examine, and to show that something is good; English prove and probe descend from it.
items.cn: 动词 probare 意为检验、考察、证明某物是好的；英语的 prove 与 probe 都由它而来。

items.en: Probabilis meant able to be approved or accepted, a claim that could pass the test, and it is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: probabilis 意为能够被认可或接受的，即经得起检验的主张，是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French borrowed the adjective as probable, meaning credible or likely, and Middle English took it over in the same shape.
items.cn: 古法语借入这个形容词写作 probable，意为可信的、很可能的，中古英语原样接收。

items.en: The adverb probably was formed with -ly and settled into its modern sense of very likely; earlier English used it more narrowly for what could be proved.
items.cn: 副词 probably 由 -ly 构成，最终固定为很可能的现代义；早期英语用它时范围更窄，专指能够被证明的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem prob- and its English shapes; the near-meaning group gathers the other adverbs English uses to hedge a claim.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁词干 prob- 及英语词形展开；近义组收英语里其他用来给判断留余地的副词。

entries.definition: Likely to be true or to happen; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能为真或发生的；副词背后的形容词。

entries.definition: How likely something is, often expressed as a number.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能程度，常用数字表示。

entries.definition: Not likely to happen or be true.
entries.definitionCN: 不大可能发生或为真的。

entries.definition: A period of testing a person's behaviour, from the same verb probare.
entries.definitionCN: 考察某人表现的一段时间，出自同一个动词 probare。

entries.definition: Used to say something may be true, with less confidence than probably.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事可能为真，把握比 probably 小。

entries.definition: Used when something can happen, even if it is not likely.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事有可能发生，即使可能性不大。

entries.definition: Expected to happen; the adjective and adverb closest in force to this word.
entries.definitionCN: 预期会发生的；语气上最接近这个词的形容词与副词。

entries.definition: Used when a conclusion is taken as true because nothing suggests otherwise.
entries.definitionCN: 在没有相反迹象时把某个结论当作成立地使用。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from a Latin verb of testing, so probably does not mean certain but has passed enough tests to be believed.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中表示检验的动词，所以 probably 不是确定，而是已经通过足够检验、可以相信。

normal.en: Probare means to test, and English prove comes from the same verb, so probable and provable began close together.
normal.cn: probare 意为检验，英语 prove 同出这一动词，所以 probable 与 provable 最初挨得很近。

normal.en: Probabilis added -bilis, the ending that means able to be, as in visible and possible.
normal.cn: probabilis 加了 -bilis，这个词尾意为能够被，和 visible、possible 里的一样。

normal.en: Probably is the adjective probable plus -ly, the standard English path from adjective to adverb.
normal.cn: probably 是形容词 probable 加 -ly，这是英语从形容词到副词的标准路径。

normal.en: Most probably and quite probably stack a degree word in front, because likelihood comes in levels.
normal.cn: most probably 与 quite probably 在前面加程度词，因为可能性是分档的。

normal.en: Improbable flips the judgement with im-, the same negative prefix as in impossible.
normal.cn: improbable 用 im- 把判断翻过来，和 impossible 里的否定前缀一样。

abstract.en: A word from the courtroom of proof ended up as the everyday adverb of guesswork, which shows how much of proof is just expectation.
abstract.cn: 一个出自证明的词，最后成了日常推测的副词，说明证明里有很大一部分不过是对结果的预期。

abstract.en: Probably never claims certainty; it measures the distance between what we know and what we say.
abstract.cn: probably 从不声称确定；它量的是我们知道多少与说出多少之间的距离。

abstract.en: Every forecast is a small bet, and this adverb is the polite way of naming the odds without handing over the money.
abstract.cn: 每一次预报都是一笔小赌注，这个副词就是礼貌地点出赔率、却不把押金交出去的方式。

examples.en: The train will probably leave from platform three.
examples.cn: 火车很可能会从三号站台开出。

examples.en: She has not answered for two days, so she is probably away.
examples.cn: 她两天没回音，想必是不在。

examples.en: It will probably rain before you reach the station.
examples.cn: 在你到车站之前多半会下雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普若巴巴利」——十有八九，嘴上还要留一点余地，就是 probably。

root: 拉丁语 probus（正直可靠的）→ probare（检验、证明）→ probabilis（经得起检验的、可信的）→ 古法语 probable → 中古英语 probable → 加 -ly 成 probably。同族还有 prove、probe、probability、probation。

sensesIntro.en: The core is tested likelihood; the senses divide by what the likelihood rests on — plain prediction, evidence already in hand, or politeness toward the listener.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是经过检验的可能性；义项按可能性的依据分开：单纯的预测、手里已有的证据，或对听者的客气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: low clouds and a hand reaching for an umbrella.
core.cn: 核心意象：云压得很低，一只手顺手拿起了伞。

branches.en: an umbrella taken on a cloudy errand
branches.cn: 阴云下出门顺手带上的伞

branches.en: an empty chair and two days of silence
branches.cn: 两天没有回音和一把空椅子

branches.en: a pause before telling someone your guess
branches.cn: 说出猜测前的那一顿

branches.en: the same caution, once about facts and once about feelings
branches.cn: 同一种谨慎，一次对事实，一次对人心

branches.en: the odds named without a promise
branches.cn: 只报赔率、不作保证的同一句话

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of proof with two English endings on top; the eight entries trace test, proof, likelihood and the adverb itself.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示证明的形容词加上两层英语词尾；下面八条依次走过检验、证明、可能性与副词本身。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb probare and the adjective probabilis are both recorded, so the English family rests on attested forms rather than on guesswork.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 probare 与形容词 probabilis 都有记录，所以这族英语词建立在有据可查的形式上，而不是猜测。

items.meaning: able to be proved or accepted

definition_zh: 难题；习题；棘手的事
definition_en: a difficulty that needs a solution, or a question to be answered in school work
core_image: 课桌上摊着算草纸，一道没解出的题被铅笔画了一个圈
scene: 课桌上摊着算草纸，一道没解出的题被铅笔画了一个圈。This maths problem is too hard for me.
sceneCN: 这里 problem 是「难题」（第 01 个义项）；句意是这道数学题对我来说太难了；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 名词：难题、习题、麻烦事

derivatives.zh: 成问题的
解决问题

senses.title: A difficulty that needs a solution
senses.definition: A difficulty that needs a solution
senses.definitionCN: 需要解决的困难
senses.example: This maths problem is too hard for me.
senses.exampleCN: 这道数学题对我来说太难了。
senses.why: Problem came from Greek problema, a thing put forward, so the word first named a question laid before someone.
senses.whyCN: problem 源自希腊语 problema（被抛出之物），最初指摆到人面前待答的问题。

senses.title: A question set for school work
senses.definition: A question set for school work
senses.definitionCN: 课业中待解的题目
senses.example: We did ten problems in class.

senses.title: A series of actions toward a result
senses.definition: a set of actions taken in order to achieve a result
senses.definitionCN: 为达到结果而按序采取的一组动作
senses.example: The hiring process takes three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘流程需要三周。
senses.why: Latin processus is 'a going forward', from procedere. A process is a path with stages: it treats time as a route to be walked.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 processus 是“向前推进”，来自 procedere。process 是一条有阶段的路：它把时间当作要走完的路线。

senses.title: A natural series of changes
senses.definition: a course of natural changes that cannot be stopped
senses.definitionCN: 无法阻止的自然变化历程
senses.example: The process of decay begins at once.
senses.exampleCN: 腐烂过程立刻开始。
senses.why: Nature supplies the purest version: growth, erosion, decay. The word describes what happens by itself, without a planner.
senses.whyCN: 自然提供最纯粹的版本：生长、侵蚀、腐烂。这个词描述自行发生、没有规划者的事。

senses.title: A manufacturing procedure
senses.definition: the set of steps by which a product is made
senses.definitionCN: 制造产品所经的一组步骤
senses.example: The new process cuts production time in half.
senses.exampleCN: 新工序把生产时间缩短一半。
senses.why: Industry systematizes the path: each step has an input, an operation, and an output. Process becomes an engineered noun, and process engineering is born.
senses.whyCN: 工业把路径系统化：每一步都有输入、操作与输出。process 成了被工程化的名词，于是有了 process engineering。

senses.title: The legal course of proceedings
senses.definition: the formal steps required by law before a decision is valid
senses.definitionCN: 决定生效前法律要求的正式步骤
senses.example: The court must follow due process.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭必须遵循正当程序。
senses.why: Due process turns the path into a guarantee: the steps are not optional, and skipping one invalidates the result. Procedure and process converge here.
senses.whyCN: 正当程序把路径变成保障：步骤不可省略，跳过一步就使结果无效。procedure 与 process 在此汇合。

senses.title: A running program (computing)
senses.definition: an instance of a program running on a computer
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中正在运行的程序实例
senses.example: The process uses most of the memory.
senses.exampleCN: 这个进程占用了大部分内存。
senses.why: An operating system schedules tasks as a series of steps. Each running instance is a process, a path being walked by the machine.
senses.whyCN: 操作系统把任务安排成一系列步骤。每个运行实例就是一个 process，一条机器正在走的路径。

senses.title: To handle by a procedure
senses.definition: to deal with information or a request according to a set method
senses.definitionCN: 按既定方法处理信息或请求
senses.example: The computer processes thousands of forms a day.
senses.exampleCN: 计算机每天处理数千份表格。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into action: to put something through the process. What is processed has entered the line and will come out changed.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：把某物送进流程。被 processed 的东西已进入流水线，出来时会变样。

senses.title: To treat food or material
senses.definition: to change a raw material by physical or chemical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 通过物理或化学处理改变原料
senses.example: The factory processes milk into cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把牛奶加工成奶酪。
senses.why: Food processing is the clearest case: the input is real, the output is real, and the stages are visible. The word carries a neutral tone, though 'processed food' can sound negative.
senses.whyCN: 食品加工是最清楚的例子：输入真实，输出真实，阶段可见。这个词语气中性，尽管 processed food 听起来可能负面。

senses.title: To move in a procession (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to walk in an ordered group
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：按队列行走
senses.example: The choir processed down the aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班列队走过通道。
senses.why: This archaic verb keeps the literal Latin walk. The noun procession is its surviving relative, still used for ceremonial lines of people.
senses.whyCN: 这个古义动词保留拉丁语字面的“走”。名词 procession 是它存活的亲戚，仍指礼仪性的人列。

senses.title: A bony projection (anatomy)
senses.definition: a natural outgrowth or prominence on a bone or organ
senses.definitionCN: 骨或器官上的自然突出部分
senses.example: The mastoid process lies behind the ear.
senses.exampleCN: 乳突位于耳后。
senses.why: Anatomy names protrusions 'processes' because they 'go forward' from the body of the bone. The Latin motion word becomes a shape word.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把突出部分称作 process，因为它们从骨体“向前伸出”。拉丁运动词变成了形状词。

intro.en: Process began as 'a going forward'. Latin processus comes from procedere, 'to advance', and English first used it for the course of events, then for industrial and legal sequences, and finally for running programs.
intro.cn: process 最初意为“向前推进”。拉丁语 processus 来自 procedere“前进”，英语先用它指事件进程，再指工业与法律序列，最后指运行中的程序。

items.en: First recorded as 'the fact of being carried on; a course of events'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“被推进的事实；事件的进程”。

items.en: From Latin processus 'a going forward, advance, progress', from procedere 'go forward'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 processus“前进、推进、进展”，源出 procedere“向前走”。

items.en: procedere = pro- 'forward' + cedere 'go'. The same verb gives proceed and procedure.
items.cn: procedere = pro-“向前”+ cedere“走”。同一动词生成 proceed 与 procedure。

items.en: The modern sense 'a continuous series of actions or changes' becomes established.
items.cn: 现代义“连续的动作或变化序列”确立。

items.en: Industrial use gives process engineering and manufacturing process.
items.cn: 工业用法产生 process engineering 与 manufacturing process。

items.en: Computing adopts the word for a running program, the newest link in the same chain.
items.cn: 计算机在 1960 年代采用这个词指运行程序，是同一链条上最新的一环。

note.en: The first group shares the cedere/procedere root; the second is about nouns that also mean a series of steps.
note.cn: 第一组共享 cedere/procedere 词根，第二组看同样表示“一系列步骤”的名词。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin procedere 'go forward', the proceed/procedure/process family, due process, and the computing sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 procedere“向前走”、proceed/procedure/process 词族、正当程序，以及计算机义。

normal.en: Processus means 'a going forward'. A process is a path with stages, walked until something comes out.
normal.cn: processus 意为“向前推进”。process 是一条有阶段的路，走到某物出来为止。

normal.en: The verb behind it is proceed: pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'go'. Process is the noun of that walk.
normal.cn: 它背后的动词是 proceed：pro-“向前”加 cedere“走”。process 是那场行走的名词。

normal.en: Procedure is a process with rules attached: the same steps, now mandatory.
normal.cn: procedure 是附上规则的 process：同样的步骤，现在成了必须。

normal.en: Due process means the steps cannot be skipped; skipping one invalidates the result.
normal.cn: 正当程序意味着步骤不可跳过；跳过一步，结果就无效。

normal.en: In computing, a process is a program mid-walk: the machine is following its steps right now.
normal.cn: 计算机中，process 是走到一半的程序：机器正在执行它的步骤。

abstract.en: A process converts time into shape: what was merely passing becomes a route with stages.
abstract.cn: 过程把时间变成形状：原本只是流逝的东西，成了有阶段的路线。

abstract.en: Calling something a process can hide responsibility: nobody did it, it just went through its steps.
abstract.cn: 把某事称作 process 可以隐藏责任：没人做的，它只是走完了步骤。

abstract.en: Nature and factory share the word because both produce an output by ordered change.
abstract.cn: 自然与工厂共享这个词，因为两者都通过有序变化产出结果。

examples.en: Learning a language is a gradual process.
examples.cn: 学语言是一个渐进的过程。

examples.en: The application process is now fully online.
examples.cn: 申请流程现已完全在线。

examples.en: The plant processes raw cocoa into chocolate.
examples.cn: 工厂把生可可加工成巧克力。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of process, one path in different costumes. The path can be natural (decay), industrial (a production line), legal (due process), digital (a running program), or even anatomical (a bony projection).
sensesIntro.cn: process 的九个义项，是同一条路的不同装扮。这条路可以是自然的（腐烂）、工业的（生产线）、法律的（正当程序）、数字的（运行程序），甚至解剖的（骨突起）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a route with stages, from input to output.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条有阶段的路，从输入到输出。

branches.en: COURSE: ordered change, whether planned or natural.
branches.cn: 历程：有序变化，无论有计划还是自然发生。

branches.en: MAKING: raw material enters a line and comes out changed.
branches.cn: 制造：原料进入流水线，出来时已变样。

branches.en: LAW: due process makes the steps mandatory and the result valid.
branches.cn: 法律：正当程序使步骤成为必须，使结果有效。

branches.en: COMPUTING: the path becomes a running program, and the verb means to put data through it.
branches.cn: 计算机：路径变成运行中的程序，动词意为让数据走一遍。

branches.en: SHAPE: the archaic walk survives in procession, while anatomy names protrusions 'processes'.
branches.cn: 形状：古义的行走存于 procession，解剖学则把突起称作 process。

intro.en: Process is noun and verb. English adds -ing, -or, and -ed, and the same Latin verb gives proceed, procedure, and procession.
intro.cn: process 既是名词也是动词。英语加 -ing、-or、-ed，同一拉丁动词还生成 proceed、procedure、procession。

latinIntro.en: Latin processus 'advance' comes from procedere 'go forward', built on cedere 'go'. The family is about ordered motion, from law courts to factory floors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 processus“推进”来自 procedere“向前走”，建立在 cedere“走”上。这个词族关乎有序运动，从法庭到工厂车间。

senses.title: Make or manufacture
senses.definition: to make something, especially in a factory or by a process

senses.example: The plant produces parts for wind turbines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂生产风力涡轮机的零件。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to lead forward, so making is bringing material forward into a finished thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向前引出」，因此制造就是把材料引成成品。

senses.title: Grow or yield from land
senses.definition: to grow crops or raise animals as a result of farming
senses.definitionCN: 通过耕作或养殖产出作物或畜禽
senses.example: The farm produces enough apples to fill a stall at the town market.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场种的苹果足够装满镇上集市的一个摊位。
senses.why: A field yielding fruit is the same bringing-forth, with land rather than a machine doing the work.

senses.title: Cause an effect
