senses.example: The new policy produced a sharp fall in complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策使投诉量大幅下降。
senses.why: Once anything can be brought forth, the word covers results that are not physical objects.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任何东西都能被「带出」，这个词便涵盖并非实物的结果。

senses.title: Show or bring forward
senses.definition: to present something for inspection, such as a document or a ticket
senses.definitionCN: 把某物拿出来供查验，如文件或票据
senses.example: The witness produced the original receipt.
senses.exampleCN: 证人出示了原始收据。
senses.why: Bringing something before someone is a literal leading forward, which explains the legal use.
senses.whyCN: 把东西带到某人面前，字面上就是「向前引出」，这解释了法律用法。

senses.title: Stage a play or film
senses.definition: to prepare and present a play, film or show for an audience
senses.definitionCN: 筹备并向观众呈现戏剧、电影或节目
senses.example: The company will produce the play in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 剧团将在春天排演这部戏。
senses.why: A show is brought out before an audience, so the cultural sense keeps the forward direction.
senses.whyCN: 一部戏被带到观众面前，因此文化义保留了「向前」的方向。

senses.title: Generate energy
senses.definition: to generate power, heat or another form of energy
senses.definitionCN: 发出电力、热量或其他形式的能量
senses.example: The dam produces power for three provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大坝为三个省发电。
senses.why: Energy is led out of a source into a usable current, which fits the word's movement image.
senses.whyCN: 能量从源头被引出成可用的电流，正合这个词的「引出」意象。

senses.title: Farm products as a mass noun
senses.titleCN: 作不可数名词指农产品
senses.definition: fresh food grown on farms, sold as a group rather than counted one by one
senses.definitionCN: 农场种出的新鲜食物，作为整体出售而非逐件计数
senses.example: The shop buys its produce from nearby growers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店从附近农户采购农产品。
senses.why: The verb's result became a collective noun for what the land brings forth.
senses.whyCN: 动词的结果转成了集合名词，指土地带出的东西。

senses.title: The fresh-food section of a shop
senses.definition: the fruit and vegetable section of a shop, or its stock
senses.definitionCN: 商店的果蔬区或其存货
senses.example: The produce aisle was restocked before opening.
senses.exampleCN: 开门前生鲜区补好了货。
senses.why: Retail narrows the collective noun to one department, the place where farm goods are sold.
senses.whyCN: 零售把集合名词收窄为一个部门，即卖农产品的地方。

intro.en: Produce comes from Latin producere 'to lead forward, bring out', through French. The noun for farm goods is a later English development of the same word.
intro.cn: produce 经法语来自拉丁 producere「向前引出、带出」；指农产品的名词义是同一词在英语中的后起发展。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw'. It gives duct, conduct, reduce and educate.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」，衍生 duct、conduct、reduce 与 educate。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere produced producere, 'to lead forward, bring out, bring forth'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere 构成 producere，意为「向前引出、带出」。

items.en: Old French produire carried the verb into English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 produire 在十五世纪把这个动词带入英语。

items.en: By the sixteenth century produce could mean bring forward a document as well as bring goods into being.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，produce 既可指造出货物，也可指出示文件。

items.en: The mass noun for crops and fresh food appeared later, first in English rather than in Latin.
items.cn: 指作物与新鲜食物的不可数名词出现更晚，是英语自身的发展而非拉丁语原有。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first date of the farm noun is not firmly recorded, and the year is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：农产品名词的最早年代没有确切记录，给出的年份只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words constantly confused with produce; group two holds near verbs for making and yielding.
note.cn: 第一组是同根且常与 produce 混淆的词；第二组是表示制造与产出的近义动词。

entries.definition: The thing made; produce as a verb makes products but never names them.
entries.definitionCN: 造出来的东西；作动词的 produce 制造产品，却不用它来指产品。

entries.definition: The activity or total output; it is what happens while produce is what is done.
entries.definitionCN: 活动或总产出；produce 是动作，production 是过程或总量。

entries.definition: The person or firm that makes; the verb names the act, not the actor.
entries.definitionCN: 制造的人或企业；动词指动作，不指施动者。

entries.definition: Re- 'again' plus produce: to make a copy or to breed; it repeats rather than originates.
entries.definitionCN: re-「再」加 produce：复制或繁殖；是重复而非原创。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for creating something; it is neutral in register where produce is formal.
entries.definitionCN: 创造某物的日常动词；语体中性，而 produce 较正式。

entries.definition: Making goods industrially; it rules out crops and effects, which produce allows.
entries.definitionCN: 工业制造货物；排除作物与结果，而 produce 都允许。

entries.definition: Producing power, data or ideas; it is close in sense three and six but rarer for goods.
entries.definitionCN: 产生电力、数据或想法；接近第 3、6 义，但少用于货物。

entries.definition: To give a crop or a result, often under pressure; it is the farming half of produce.
entries.definitionCN: 出产作物或结果，常含受压之意；是 produce 中务农的一半。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the lead-forward root, the mass noun and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「向前引出」词根、不可数名词与固定搭配。

normal.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'lead': to produce is to lead something into being.
normal.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere「引导」：produce 就是把某物引出来。

normal.en: The family runs produce, product, production, producer, productive and reproduce.
normal.cn: 同族词有 produce、product、production、producer、productive 与 reproduce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: produce evidence, produce results, farm produce, locally produced.
normal.cn: 固定说法：出示证据、产生结果、农产品、本地生产的。

normal.en: The noun shifts its stress to the first syllable, which is how English marks the change of word class.
normal.cn: 作名词时重音移到第一音节，这是英语标记词性变化的方式。

normal.en: The same root appears in conduct, introduce, reduce and educate.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educate 中。

abstract.en: Picture a tree handing fruit into a basket one branch at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树一根枝一根枝地把果子交进篮子。

abstract.en: Picture a document sliding across a desk to be checked.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件在桌面上滑过去接受查验。

abstract.en: Picture a switch that turns a river's weight into light in a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个开关，把河流的重量变进房间的灯光。

examples.en: The region produces more olive oil than it can sell at home.
examples.cn: 该地区生产的橄榄油超过本地能卖出的量。

examples.en: The lawyer asked the company to produce the missing records.
examples.cn: 律师要求公司出示缺失的记录。

examples.en: A single change in the wording produced a very different response.
examples.cn: 措辞上的一处改动引出了很不一样的反应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ duce（引导）」——把东西一路引出来，就是生产与出产

root: 拉丁 producere「向前引出、带出」= pro-（向前）+ ducere「引导」；经古法语 produire 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bringing-forth: manufacturing, farming, causing an effect, showing a document, staging a show, generating power, farm goods as a mass noun and finally the shop's fresh section.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「带出」这个动作：制造、种出、引起结果、出示文件、排演、发电、作不可数名词指农产品，最后是商店的生鲜区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket of picked fruit carrying a label that says where it grew.
core.cn: 核心意象：一篮摘下的果子，标签上写着它长在哪里。

branches.en: MAKING AND GROWING: a factory line and a field are both ways of leading material into a result.
branches.cn: 制造与种植：工厂流水线与田地，都是把材料引成结果的方式。

branches.en: BROUGHT FORTH: an effect and a document are both brought forward where they can be seen.
branches.cn: 被带出：结果与文件都被带到能被看见的地方。

branches.en: STAGE AND SHOP: a show and a fresh-food aisle are places where produce is presented to the public.
branches.cn: 舞台与店铺：演出与生鲜区，都是把出产呈现给公众的场所。

branches.en: POWER: energy is led out of a source into a current.
branches.cn: 电力：能量从源头被引出成电流。

branches.en: MASS NOUN: what the land brings forth becomes a collective name for food.
branches.cn: 集合名词：土地带出的东西成了食物的统称。

intro.en: Produce is a Latin verb of leading forward, and its prefix and root still build a large English family.
intro.cn: produce 是表示「向前引出」的拉丁动词，其前缀与词根仍构成一大片英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere gives conduct, introduce, reduce and educate; pro- adds the forward direction kept in produce.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educate；pro- 增添 produce 保留的向前方向。

items.example: The prefix points the action outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向外。

items.example: The product sells in six countries.

senses.title: What a chemical reaction makes
senses.titleCN: 化学反应生成的新物质
senses.definition: a substance formed when other substances react
senses.definitionCN: 由其他物质发生反应后生成的新物质
senses.example: Water is the product of the reaction between hydrogen and oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 水是氢与氧反应的生成物。
senses.why: the word is the past participle of a Latin verb meaning to lead forth, so a product is literally what has been brought out of a process.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是拉丁动词「引出」的过去分词，因此 product 字面就是「被过程带出来的东西」。

senses.title: A thing made for sale
senses.definition: an item manufactured or grown in order to be sold
senses.definitionCN: 为出售而制造或种植的物品
senses.example: The company moved its best product to the front of the catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把最好的产品移到目录前页。
senses.why: commerce narrowed the general sense of what is brought forth to what is brought forth for a buyer.
senses.whyCN: 商业把「被带出来的东西」这一通义收窄为「为买家带出来的东西」。

senses.title: A result of effort
senses.definition: an outcome of work, thinking or events, often abstract
senses.definitionCN: 工作、思考或事件带来的结果，常为抽象之物
senses.example: The report was the product of three years of fieldwork.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是三年野外工作的成果。
senses.why: if a process brings something out, anything brought out counts, including knowledge and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 只要过程能带出东西，被带出的一切都算，包括知识与制度。

senses.title: The result of multiplication
senses.definition: the number obtained by multiplying two or more numbers
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个数相乘所得的数
senses.example: The product of six and seven is forty-two.
senses.exampleCN: 六与七的乘积是四十二。
senses.why: mathematics borrowed the same participle: multiplication brings forth a number from two others.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用了同一个分词：乘法从两个数里带出一个数。

senses.title: A child of its time or place
senses.definition: a person or thing shaped entirely by a particular background
senses.definitionCN: 完全由某一背景塑造的人或事物
senses.example: He was a product of the same crowded schools he later criticized.
senses.exampleCN: 他正是他后来批评的那种拥挤学校的产物。
senses.why: the metaphor says that circumstances manufacture people in the way a factory manufactures goods.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻说环境造人，正如工厂造货。

senses.title: Farm output
senses.definition: crops or other goods grown from the land, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 地里种出的作物等物产，常用复数
senses.example: The market sells local products from the surrounding farms.
senses.exampleCN: 这个市场出售周边农场的本地农产品。
senses.why: farming speaks of its output as produce, and the plural products marks things grown rather than made.
senses.whyCN: 农业把自己的产出说成 produce，复数 products 标记的是种出来的东西，而非造出来的。

senses.title: A work of media or art
senses.titleCN: 媒体或艺术作品的产物
senses.definition: a film, recording or other creative work considered as an item made by a studio
senses.definitionCN: 被视为由制片机构制作的电影、录音等创作成品
senses.example: The studio treats every film as a product with a release date.
senses.exampleCN: 制片方把每部电影都当作有发行日期的产品。
senses.why: the entertainment industry uses the commercial sense of the word, so a film becomes a product beside toys and tickets.
senses.whyCN: 娱乐业使用这个词的商业义，于是电影与玩具、门票并列成为产品。

senses.title: One item in a brand range
senses.titleCN: 品牌系列中的单个品项
senses.definition: a single item within a company's range, tracked separately in sales and marketing
senses.definitionCN: 公司系列中的单个品项，在销售与营销中单独核算
senses.example: Each product in the range has its own price and its own page.
senses.exampleCN: 系列中的每个产品都有自己的价格与页面。
senses.why: marketing splits a range into countable units, and the word becomes the unit of accounting rather than the whole output.
senses.whyCN: 营销把一个系列拆成可数的单位，这个词于是成为核算单位，而不是全部产出。

intro.en: Product comes from Latin productum, the neuter past participle of producere, to lead forth, built on pro-, forward, and ducere, to lead. It entered English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: product 出自拉丁语 productum，即 producere「引出」的中性过去分词；该动词由 pro-「向前」与 ducere「引导」构成。它在 16 世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead, draw or guide; its past participle ductum supplied a long series of English words. The deeper Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉、带领」，其过去分词 ductum 提供了一长串英语词。更早的印欧词根属于重构。

items.en: Pro-, forward, plus ducere produced producere, to lead forth, bring out, extend, which is the source of produce, product and production.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere 构成 producere「引出、带出、延长」，是 produce、product 与 production 的来源。

items.en: The neuter participle productum came to be used as a noun for something brought out or brought forth, the direct model of the English word.
items.cn: 中性分词 productum 被当作名词使用，指被带出、被产生的东西，是英语词的直接样板。

items.en: Product entered English in the sixteenth century, first as a general word for a result and also as the mathematical term for the result of multiplication.
items.cn: product 于 16 世纪进入英语，最初泛指结果，同时也是表示乘法结果的数学术语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the commercial sense of a manufactured item for sale became dominant, and the plural products spread into farming and marketing.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，指供出售的制成品这一商业义占据主导，复数形式 products 又扩散到农业与营销。

items.en: First date uncertain: the century of entry is well attested, but the earliest citation of the commercial sense is not settled, so the date given for that sense is approximate.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：进入英语的世纪有可靠记载，但商业义的最早书证尚无定论，因此为该义给出的年代只是约数。

note.en: The first group shares the produce stem; the second group names other results and other stages of making something.
note.cn: 第一组共享 produce 词干；第二组是其他表示结果或制作阶段的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to bring forth; its noun form, pronounced differently, means fresh farm goods as a mass.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「产生、生产」的动词；其名词形式读音不同，指作为整体的新鲜农产品。

entries.definition: The activity or amount of making things; a product is the thing, production is the making of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指制作活动或产量；product 是物，production 是制作这件事。

entries.definition: Something made incidentally while the main product is being made; it is not the intended output.
entries.definitionCN: 在制造主要产品时顺带产生的东西，不是有意要的产出。

entries.definition: The person or firm that makes the product; the -er ending marks the maker rather than the made.
entries.definitionCN: 制作产品的人或公司；词尾 -er 标记制作者，而不是被制作之物。

entries.definition: The general word for what follows from something; it does not imply that the thing was made or sold.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指由某事带来的结果；不含「被制造或被出售」的意思。

entries.definition: What a system turns out, often measured as a rate or total; it stresses quantity more than the item itself.
entries.definitionCN: 系统产出的东西，常以速率或总量计量；强调数量多过单件物品。

entries.definition: The amount obtained from a process, especially a reaction or a field; chemistry counts yield, not products alone.
entries.definitionCN: 从过程得到的量，尤指反应或田地；化学算的是收率，而不只是产物本身。

entries.definition: Movable items for sale, always plural; it is a commercial collective, while product can name one item.
entries.definitionCN: 可供出售的动产，总用复数；它是商业集合名词，而 product 可以指单件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real word family and real commercial phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的同族词与真实的商业说法。

normal.en: Pro- forward plus ducere to lead: to lead something out of a process.
normal.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere「引导」：把某物从过程中引出来。

normal.en: The family runs produce, product, production, productive, productivity and producer.
normal.cn: 同族词有 produce、product、production、productive、productivity 与 producer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the commercial sense: product line, product launch, final product.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出商业义：产品线、产品发布、成品。

normal.en: The same word serves the reaction and the multiplication, which is why chemistry and arithmetic share it.
normal.cn: 同一个词既服务反应也服务乘法，所以化学与算术共用它。

normal.en: Product and by-product differ by one prefix: the second is what came out although nobody planned it.
normal.cn: product 与 by-product 只差一个前缀：后者是没人计划却照样出来的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a conveyor belt that ends exactly where the empty crates begin.
abstract.cn: 想象一条传送带的终点，正好是空料箱开始的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a child who repeats the habits of a school he later argues against.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子，重复着他后来反对的那所学校的习惯。

abstract.en: Picture two numbers meeting and leaving one number behind.
abstract.cn: 想象两个数相遇，留下一个数。

examples.en: The reaction produces a gas as its main product.
examples.cn: 这个反应的主要产物是一种气体。

examples.en: A product that nobody can repair will not keep its buyers.
examples.cn: 无人能修的产品留不住买家。

examples.en: The product of the two lengths gives the area of the rectangle.
examples.cn: 两条边的乘积给出矩形的面积。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ duct（引导）」——把东西往前带出来的结果 → 产品、产物

root: 拉丁 ducere「引导」→ pro- 加 ducere 成 producere「引出」→ 过去分词 productum → 英语 product「被带出的东西」；16 世纪进入英语，商业义确切首见年代无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: something is led out of a process. The act then serves a reaction, a factory, a piece of work, a multiplication, a whole era, a farm, a studio and finally one shelf item.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：某物被从过程中引出来。这个动作随后服务于反应、工厂、一项工作、一次乘法、一个时代、一片农田、一家制片机构，最后是货架上的一个单品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the end of a conveyor belt where a finished object drops into a tray beside empty crates.
core.cn: 核心意象：传送带的尽头，一件成品落进托盘，旁边是空了的料箱。

branches.en: THE REACTION OUTPUT: a new substance appears where two others met.
branches.cn: 反应产出：两种物质相遇之处出现一种新物质。

branches.en: THE SHELF: a made item, and then one countable item inside a range.
branches.cn: 货架：一件制成品，再细化为系列中可数的一个单品。

branches.en: WORK AND MEDIA: knowledge, reports and films are brought out like goods.

senses.title: Relating to a profession
senses.definition: connected with a profession or its members
senses.definitionCN: 与某个职业或其成员相关
senses.example: professional bodies set entry exams.
senses.exampleCN: 行业机构设置入行考试。
senses.why: Profession comes from Latin professio, 'a public declaration'. A professional was first someone who had publicly declared a calling, which is why the word implies a recognized field.
senses.whyCN: profession 来自拉丁语 professio“公开宣告”。professional 最初指公开宣告某种志业的人，所以这个词隐含一个被承认的领域。

senses.title: Done as a paid occupation
senses.definition: engaged in for payment rather than as a hobby
senses.definitionCN: 为报酬而从事，而非作为爱好
senses.example: She is a professional musician.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一名职业音乐家。
senses.why: The 18c. sharpened the contrast with amateur: a professional is paid, an amateur is not. Money becomes the marker that separates the two.
senses.whyCN: 18 世纪强化了与 amateur 的对比：professional 拿钱，业余者不拿。金钱成了区分两者的标记。

senses.title: Competent and skillful
senses.definition: showing the skill and care expected of a trained person
senses.definitionCN: 表现出受训者应有的技能与用心
senses.example: That was a very professional repair job.
senses.exampleCN: 那次维修做得非常专业。
senses.why: Skill turns the label into a compliment: work is professional when it meets the standard a paying client would expect. The word moves from status to quality.
senses.whyCN: 技能把这个标签变成赞美：当工作达到付费客户期待的标准，它就是专业的。这个词从身份转向品质。

senses.title: A member of a profession
senses.definition: a person who works in a profession, especially a learned one
senses.definitionCN: 从事某一职业的人，尤指需要专门学识者
senses.example: The panel included doctors and other professionals.
senses.exampleCN: 专家组包括医生及其他专业人员。
senses.why: The noun names the person behind the adjective. In modern English it often covers lawyers, doctors, engineers, and accountants — fields with entry rules and codes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名形容词背后的人。现代英语中它常涵盖律师、医生、工程师、会计师——有准入规则与职业准则的领域。

senses.title: An expert in a field
senses.definition: a person with high skill in some activity
senses.definitionCN: 在某项活动中技能很高的人
senses.example: He is a professional when it comes to chess.
senses.exampleCN: 在国际象棋上他是个行家。
senses.why: The word can leave the salaried professions behind and simply mean 'someone who really knows'. This looser use turns expertise itself into the qualification.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以离开领薪的职业，只表示“真正懂行的人”。这种宽松用法把专长本身当成资格。

senses.title: A paid sports player
senses.definition: in sport, a player who is paid to compete
senses.definitionCN: 体育中受薪参赛的选手
senses.example: He turned professional at nineteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十九岁转为职业选手。
senses.why: Sport copied the paid/amateur divide. Turning professional means crossing a line: from playing for love to playing for a living, with different rules and stakes.
senses.whyCN: 体育复制了“受薪／业余”的分界。转为职业，意味着跨过一条线：从为热爱而赛，到为生计而赛，规则与利害都不同。

senses.title: Conforming to professional standards
senses.definition: behaving with the ethics and manners of a profession
senses.definitionCN: 以某职业的伦理与礼节行事
senses.example: Her response was calm and professional.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回应冷静而专业。
senses.why: Conduct is judged, not skill. The word can praise someone who keeps confidences and meets deadlines, even when the task is routine.
senses.whyCN: 这里被评判的是行为，不是技能。即使任务平常，这个词也能赞美守密、守时的人。

senses.title: Of high quality, informally
senses.definition: in informal use, well-made or impressive
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法：做得好的、像样的
senses.example: They did a professional job on the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把花园弄得相当像样。
senses.why: The compliment has spread beyond occupations: anything done with care can look professional. The word now sells quality as much as status.
senses.whyCN: 这种赞美已超出职业范围：任何用心做成的事都可能显得 professional。这个词现在既卖身份，也卖品质。

senses.title: A euphemism for a sex worker (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, a euphemism for a prostitute
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：对妓女的委婉说法
senses.example: The old novel refers to her as a professional.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧小说用 professional 指称她。
senses.why: The 'paid occupation' sense sits close to a taboo, so the euphemism was available. Modern usage avoids it because the main sense has become too respectable to carry the hint.
senses.whyCN: “受薪职业”义接近禁忌，因此这个委婉说法曾可用。现代用法避开它，因为主要义已太体面，承载不了这层暗示。

intro.en: Professional is built on profession, and profession began as a public declaration. Latin profiteri means 'declare openly', from pro- 'forth' plus fateri 'to confess'. A professional is, etymologically, someone who has declared what they do.
intro.cn: professional 建立在 profession 上，而 profession 始于“公开宣告”。拉丁语 profiteri 意为“公开宣称”，由 pro-“向前、出来”加 fateri“承认”构成。从词源看，professional 就是公开宣告自己以何为业的人。

items.en: First recorded as an adjective meaning 'of or belonging to a profession'.
items.cn: 最早记录为形容词，义为“属于某一职业的”。

items.en: profession (late 14c.) comes from Latin professionem, 'a public declaration', from profiteri 'declare openly'.
items.cn: profession（14 世纪末）来自拉丁语 professionem“公开宣告”，源出 profiteri“公开宣称”。

items.en: profiteri = pro- 'forth, publicly' + fateri 'to confess, admit'. The root fateri also gives confession and fate in related senses.
items.cn: profiteri = pro-“向外、公开”+ fateri“承认、告白”。词根 fateri 还生成 confession 等相关词。

items.en: The sense 'engaged in a profession as a paid calling' is recorded.
items.cn: “以某职业为受薪志业”的义项被记录。

items.en: The noun professional appears for a person who makes a living by a profession.
items.cn: 名词 professional 出现，指以某职业谋生的人。

items.en: Modern English extends the adjective from occupations to quality and conduct: professional advice, professional standards, a professional job.
items.cn: 现代英语把形容词从职业扩展到品质与行为：professional advice、professional standards、a professional job。

note.en: The first group shares the profession/profiteri stem; the second is about words that also mean skilled or paid.
note.cn: 第一组共享 profession/profiteri 词干，第二组看同样表示“有技能”或“受薪”的词。

entries.definition: a paid occupation requiring training. It is the noun behind professional.
entries.definitionCN: 需要训练的受薪职业。它是 professional 背后的名词。

entries.definition: the standards and conduct of a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 职业标准与职业精神。

entries.definition: a university teacher, literally one who professes a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 大学教授，字面“宣称某学科者”。

entries.definition: a person with special knowledge. It stresses knowledge, not pay or code.
entries.definitionCN: 有专门知识的人。它强调知识，而非报酬或准则。

entries.definition: having trained ability. It says nothing about a profession or payment.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、有能力。它不涉及职业或报酬。

entries.definition: relating to a job. It is neutral and technical, unlike the status-laden professional.
entries.definitionCN: 与工作相关的。它中性、技术性，不像 professional 带身份色彩。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin profiteri 'declare openly', the paid/amateur divide, the professional/professor family, and the modern quality sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 profiteri“公开宣称”、受薪／业余之分、professional/professor 词族，以及现代品质义。

normal.en: Latin profiteri means 'declare openly': a professional has publicly declared what they do.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 profiteri 意为“公开宣称”：professional 已公开宣告自己以何为业。

normal.en: The 18c. made money the test: professionals are paid, amateurs are not.
normal.cn: 18 世纪以金钱为标准：professional 受薪，业余者不受薪。

normal.en: Professor and professional share the root: both publicly profess a field.
normal.cn: professor 与 professional 共享词根：两者都公开宣称某个领域。

normal.en: The word has moved from status to quality: a professional job is simply a job done to a high standard.
normal.cn: 这个词从身份滑向品质：a professional job 就是做得高标准的工作。

normal.en: In sport, turning professional means crossing from playing for love to playing for a living.
normal.cn: 体育中，转为职业意味着从为热爱而赛，跨到为生计而赛。

abstract.en: A profession is a public promise: the declaration is what binds the practitioner to a code.
abstract.cn: 职业是一份公开承诺：宣告把从业者绑定到一套准则上。

abstract.en: Professionalism is a form of trust infrastructure: strangers can rely on you because a field vouches for you.
abstract.cn: 专业精神是一种信任基础设施：陌生人能依赖你，因为一个领域为你背书。

abstract.en: When the word praises quality rather than occupation, it shows how deeply work and identity are fused in modern life.
abstract.cn: 当这个词赞美品质而非职业时，它显示出工作与身份在现代生活中融合得有多深。

examples.en: You should seek professional advice before investing.
examples.cn: 投资前你应当寻求专业建议。

examples.en: She handled the complaint in a professional manner.
examples.cn: 她以专业的方式处理了这起投诉。

examples.en: He became a professional football player at twenty.
examples.cn: 他二十岁时成为职业足球运动员。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of professional, all built on a public declaration. The declaration can name an occupation, mark payment, certify skill, impose conduct, or simply advertise quality.
sensesIntro.cn: professional 的九个义项都建立在一次公开宣告上。这次宣告可以命名职业、标记受薪、证明技能、施加行为准则，或仅仅为品质作广告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a public declaration that binds a person to a standard.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次公开宣告，把人绑定到某个标准上。

branches.en: FIELD: a recognized occupation and the people who belong to it.
branches.cn: 领域：被承认的职业及其成员。

branches.en: PAY: the paid/amateur line, in work and in sport.
branches.cn: 报酬：工作与体育中的受薪／业余分界。

branches.en: SKILL: training shows as competence, and competence can stand alone as expertise.
branches.cn: 技能：训练表现为胜任，胜任又可单独成为专长。

branches.en: ETHICS: conduct is judged by the standards of the field.
branches.cn: 伦理：行为按该领域的标准被评判。

branches.en: EXTENSIONS: informal praise of quality, and an archaic euphemism that the main sense has outgrown.
branches.cn: 延伸：对品质的非正式赞美，以及主要义已使其不再适用的旧委婉语。

intro.en: Professional is profession plus -al. English adds -ly, -ism, -ize, and the negative un-, while the Latin fateri also gives confess and confession.
intro.cn: professional 是 profession 加 -al。英语加 -ly、-ism、-ize 与否定 un-，拉丁语 fateri 还生成 confess 与 confession。

latinIntro.en: Latin professio 'public declaration' and profiteri 'declare openly' combine pro- 'forth' with fateri 'admit'. The family is about public avowal, not merely employment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 professio“公开宣告”与 profiteri“公开宣称”把 pro-“向外”与 fateri“承认”结合。这个词族关乎公开表态，而不只是就业。

senses.title: A senior university teacher with a chair or high post
senses.definition: a university teacher of the highest rank, usually holding a chair in a subject
senses.definitionCN: 大学中等级最高的教师，通常在某学科拥有教席
senses.example: She was made a professor at thirty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 她三十五岁时被聘为教授。
senses.why: The Latin word was simply a person who declares publicly; the medieval university gave that declarer a fixed place and rank, and the title followed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本只是「公开发言的人」；中世纪的大学给这种公开讲授者固定的位置与等级，教授这一头衔便由此而来。

senses.title: A title placed before a name
senses.definition: a title used before the name of someone who holds such a post
senses.definitionCN: 用在拥有该职位者姓名之前的称呼
senses.example: Professor Lane will see you now.
senses.exampleCN: 莱恩教授现在可以见你了。
senses.why: Once the post became recognised, the name of the post turned into a form of address, shortened in speech but kept whole in writing.
senses.whyCN: 职位一旦被公认，职位的名称就变成了对人的称呼；口语里常简化，书面里仍写全。

senses.title: Any teacher at an American college
senses.definition: in American usage, a teacher at a college or university of any rank
senses.definitionCN: 在美式用法中，指学院或大学里任何级别的教师
senses.example: My professor assigned two chapters for Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 我的老师布置了周五要读的两章。
senses.why: American campuses applied the grand title to ordinary instructors, so the word widened from the chair-holder to almost anyone who teaches there.
senses.whyCN: 美国校园把这一显赫头衔套在普通讲师身上，于是词义从「拥有教席者」扩大到几乎所有在那里教书的人。

senses.title: A person who declares a belief publicly
senses.titleCN: 公开宣称者；信仰表白者
senses.definition: a person who makes an open declaration, especially of religious faith
senses.definitionCN: 公开做出声明的人，尤指公开表白宗教信仰者
senses.example: The early professors of the faith met in secret.
senses.exampleCN: 早期公开表白信仰的人秘密聚会。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin sense, still visible in the word's shape: the professor is the one who professes.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语的字面义，今天仍能从词的构造看出来：professor 就是「做公开声明的那个人」。

intro.en: Professor and profession share one Latin verb: profession names the declared work, while professor names the person who declares it.
intro.cn: professor 与 profession 共用一个拉丁动词：profession 指被声明的工作，professor 则指做声明的人。

items.en: Fateri meant to confess or acknowledge, to say openly something about oneself.
items.cn: fateri 意为承认、供认，即公开说出关于自己的事。

items.en: With pro-, the verb became profiteri, to declare publicly, whether a belief or a calling.
items.cn: 加上前缀 pro-，动词成为 profiteri，意为公开声明，对象可以是信仰，也可以是志业。

items.en: Professor was the agent noun: the person who professes, who declares openly, often a teacher of a doctrine.
items.cn: professor 是施动名词：做公开声明的人，常指某学说的讲授者。

items.en: In the medieval university a professor was one who publicly taught and disputed, and the word became tied to a teaching post.
items.cn: 在中世纪大学里，professor 指公开讲授并参与论辩的人，这个词遂与教职绑定。

items.en: English kept the academic sense as the main one, widened it in America to any college teacher, and let the religious sense fade.
items.cn: 英语以学术义为主，又在美国用法中扩大到任何大学教师，宗教义则逐渐淡去。

note.en: The first group is the same Latin family, including the noun for the declared work; the second gathers words for people who teach.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词族，包括指「被声明的工作」的那个名词；第二组收表示教书育人之人的词。

entries.definition: To declare openly that one holds a belief or does a kind of work.
entries.definitionCN: 公开声明自己持某种信念或从事某种工作。

entries.definition: The declared work or calling, rather than the person who declares it.
entries.definitionCN: 被公开认领的职业或志业，指事不指人。

entries.definition: Relating to a profession, or a person who works in one.
entries.definitionCN: 与职业有关的；从事某一职业的人。

entries.definition: A person who confesses, or a priest who hears confession.
entries.definitionCN: 忏悔者；听人告解的司铎。

entries.definition: A teacher at a university below professorial rank.
entries.definitionCN: 大学中低于教授级别的教师；讲师。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to help others learn.
entries.definitionCN: 以帮助他人学习为业的人。

entries.definition: A person who teaches or researches at a university.
entries.definitionCN: 在大学任教或做研究的人。

entries.definition: A person who studies a subject deeply.

normalIntro.en: The word is the agent noun of a Latin verb of public declaring, and its history runs from the street speaker to the university chair.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「公开声明」动词的施动名词，它的历史从街头的发言者一路走到大学的教席。

normal.en: Professor ends in -or, the Latin ending for the doer, so it means the one who professes.
normal.cn: professor 以 -or 结尾，这是拉丁语表示「做事者」的词尾，所以它指「做声明的人」。

normal.en: The verb behind it is profiteri, to declare openly; a professor is literally a public declarer.
normal.cn: 背后的动词是 profiteri，意为公开声明；professor 字面上就是「公开声明者」。

normal.en: Profession is the declared work, professor the declarer, so the two words split one idea into thing and person.
normal.cn: profession 是被声明的工作，professor 是声明者，两个词把同一个意思拆成了「事」与「人」。

normal.en: The academic sense grew in medieval universities, where teaching was a public act of declaring a doctrine.
normal.cn: 学术义在中世纪大学里长成，因为当时的讲课就是公开声明某种学说的行为。

normal.en: In America the title spread to all college teachers, which is why students there call any instructor professor.
normal.cn: 在美国，这一头衔扩散到所有大学教师，所以那里的学生管任何讲师都叫 professor。

abstract.en: A professor is proof that teaching was once a form of public speech, not a private exchange of notes.
abstract.cn: professor 证明教学曾经是一种公开言说，而不是私下交换笔记。

abstract.en: The same root ties the classroom to the pulpit: to profess was first to declare a faith aloud.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根把课堂与讲坛系在一起：profess 最初就是大声宣告信仰。

abstract.en: A title that once meant one who speaks in public now marks one who is allowed to be heard.
abstract.cn: 这个头衔原指在公众面前说话的人，如今标记的是「有资格被听见」的人。

examples.en: The professor answered questions for ten minutes before the lecture.
examples.cn: 教授在开讲前回答了十分钟问题。

examples.en: Professor Hall has taught chemistry here for twenty years.
examples.cn: 霍尔教授在这里教了二十年化学。

examples.en: He was appointed professor of history last autumn.
examples.cn: 他去年秋天被聘为历史学教授。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「铺若费舌」——教授在讲台上把知识铺开，费尽口舌；记住 professor 是教授。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（公开、向前）+ fateri（承认）→ profiteri（公开声明）→ professor（公开宣称者，后指公开讲授者），经中世纪大学用语进入英语；与 profession 同源，一为「声明/职业」，一为「声明者」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the person who declares publicly; the academic post, the title before a name, the American widening and the old religious declarer all branch from that figure.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「公开做声明的人」；学术职位、姓名前的称谓、美式用法的扩大，以及旧时的宗教宣称者，都从这个人影分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scholar behind a lectern, declaring a subject aloud to a room of listeners.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位学者站在讲台后，当众向满屋听众讲明一门学问。

branches.en: a chair-holder whose name is spoken with a title
branches.cn: 拥有教席、名字前带称谓的人

branches.en: a lecture hall filling before the first word
branches.cn: 开讲之前逐渐坐满的讲堂

branches.en: a student asking any instructor for help
branches.cn: 学生向任何一位讲师求助

branches.cn: 一小群人在暗中表白信仰

branches.en: a name card reading professor at the top
branches.cn: 名片最上方印着教授字样

intro.en: A Latin verb of public declaring, its prefix and its agent ending, plus the English endings that turn the person into a post and a quality, hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示公开声明的拉丁动词、它的前缀与施动词尾，再加上把「人」变成职位与性质的英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

senses.title: A plan of future action
senses.definition: a set of intended actions arranged in advance to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 为了达到某个目标而事先安排好的一系列行动
senses.example: The city launched a housing program for low-income families.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府启动了一项面向低收入家庭的住房计划。
senses.why: the Greek noun began as a public notice written down ahead of time, so the word still carries the idea of something laid out before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词最初指事先写好的公开通告，因此这个词始终带着「事情发生之前就摆好的安排」这一层意思。

senses.title: An order of events
senses.definition: a list showing the times and order of the parts of an event
senses.definitionCN: 列出活动各部分时间与顺序的清单
senses.example: The conference program lists every talk and the room it uses.
senses.exampleCN: 会议日程列出了每场报告及其所在房间。
senses.why: a written notice of what will happen and when is the most literal survival of the original sense.
senses.whyCN: 把「将发生什么、何时发生」写下来通告，正是原义最直接的延续。

senses.title: A printed list for an audience
senses.definition: the printed sheet given to an audience, naming the performers and the works
senses.definitionCN: 发给观众、写明演出者与曲目的印刷纸页
senses.example: She read the program before the orchestra tuned up.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团调音之前，她先读了节目单。
senses.why: theatres turned the order of a performance into a small printed booklet, and the booklet took the name of the order itself.
senses.whyCN: 剧院把演出顺序做成一本小册子，册子便直接沿用了「顺序」这个名字。

senses.title: A show that is broadcast
senses.definition: a single show or an ongoing series carried by a station
senses.definitionCN: 由电台或电视台播出的单个节目或系列节目
senses.example: The station dropped the program after one season.
senses.exampleCN: 电视台播出一季后停掉了这个节目。
senses.why: broadcasting inherited the word from theatre: each slot in the schedule is a program, whether or not paper is involved.
senses.whyCN: 广播沿用了剧院的说法：节目表上的每一个时段都叫一个节目，与纸张已无关系。

senses.title: Instructions a computer follows
senses.definition: an ordered set of coded instructions that makes a computer carry out a task
senses.definitionCN: 使计算机完成一项任务的有序编码指令集合
senses.example: The program sorts the files by date and deletes the copies.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序按日期排序文件并删除重复副本。
senses.why: the earliest electronic machines were fed a written sequence of steps, exactly like a plan handed to a reader, so the plan word moved onto the machine.
senses.whyCN: 最早的电子机器接收的是一份写好的步骤序列，就像交给读者的一份计划，于是「计划」这个词就移到了机器上。

senses.title: A course of study
senses.definition: an organized course or set of courses leading to a qualification
senses.definitionCN: 通向某种资格的有组织课程或课程组合
senses.example: The new program leads to a master's degree in two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新课程两年后可获硕士学位。
senses.why: schools borrowed the plan word because a degree is also a sequence of steps that a student is expected to complete in order.
senses.whyCN: 学校借用了「计划」这个词，因为拿学位同样是一串要求学生按顺序完成的步骤。

senses.title: A government or agency scheme
senses.definition: an official scheme that organizes money and staff for a public purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为公共目的组织资金与人员的官方方案
senses.example: The literacy program trained teachers in three rural counties.
senses.exampleCN: 这项扫盲计划在三个农村县培训了教师。
senses.why: public bodies write down what they intend to do and fund it, and that funded intention is called a program.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构把打算做的事写下来并拨款，这份带钱的打算就被称为项目。

senses.title: To set something to happen
senses.definition: to arrange for a device or system to act at a set time or in a set way
senses.definitionCN: 安排某个设备或系统在固定时间或以固定方式动作
senses.example: They programmed the lights to switch off at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把灯设定在午夜自动关闭。
senses.why: once a machine can hold its own sequence of steps, the verb means putting that sequence into it, even when no code is written by hand.
senses.whyCN: 一旦机器能自己保存步骤序列，动词就表示把序列装进去，哪怕并没有手写代码。

senses.title: To write instructions for a machine
senses.definition: to write the code that a computer or machine will execute
senses.definitionCN: 编写计算机或机器将要执行的代码
senses.example: He programmed the robot to pick only the ripe fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 他给机器人编程，让它只摘成熟的果子。
senses.why: this is the modern verb built directly on the computing noun: the programmer writes the plan the machine will follow.
senses.whyCN: 这是直接由计算机义名词转来的现代动词：程序员写下机器将要遵循的计划。

intro.en: Program is Greek in origin, Latin in transmission and French in form. Its oldest sense is a public notice written in advance; the computing sense is a twentieth-century extension. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: program 源于希腊语，经拉丁语传递，形式取自法语。它最古老的意思是事先写好的公开通告；计算机义是二十世纪的延伸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek programma meant a public written notice, built from pro-, before, and graphein, to write. The noun named a posted announcement, not a scheme of action.
items.cn: 希腊语 programma 指公开的书面通告，由 pro-「在前」与 graphein「书写」构成。这个名词指的是张贴出来的公告，而不是行动计划。

items.en: Latin borrowed programma as a learned noun for a written notice or preface, keeping the Greek shape and the written, public flavour.
items.cn: 拉丁语借用 programma 作为书面通告或序言的学术名词，保留了希腊语的形式与「书面、公开」的色彩。

items.en: French programme entered English in the seventeenth century. English first used it for a public notice and soon for the printed order of a ceremony or performance.
items.cn: 法语 programme 在十七世纪进入英语。英语先用它指公开通告，很快又用它指仪式或演出的印刷顺序。

items.en: American printers shortened the ending to program. The two spellings now divide mainly by region, and the short form became standard in computing.
items.cn: 美国印刷者把词尾缩短为 program。两种拼写如今基本按地区分工，而短形式在计算机领域成为标准。

items.en: From the 1940s a program meant the coded sequence that drives a machine. The noun, and then the verb to program, followed the hardware into ordinary use.
items.cn: 自 1940 年代起，program 指驱动机器的编码序列。名词以及后来的动词「编程」随硬件一起进入日常使用。

items.en: The chain from Greek programma through Latin programma and French programme to English program is documented. Only the first written dates in English are approximate, and any Indo-European root proposed for graphein is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：从希腊语 programma 经拉丁语 programma、法语 programme 到英语的这条链有文献依据，只是英语最早书证的年代为约数；为 graphein 提出的印欧语词根属于重构形式，并非有记录的词。

note.en: The first group is the same word in other shapes and roles; the second group names neighbouring ideas of a plan, a timetable and software.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的其他形式与角色；第二组是与计划、时间表和软件相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same noun, and the usual form for a printed list of performances; computing writing prefers program everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个名词的英式拼写，也是节目单的常用形式；计算机写作各地多用 program。

entries.definition: The activity of writing code, not the code of one task; the noun names the work, while program names the product.
entries.definitionCN: 指编写代码这项活动，而不是某一任务的代码；名词指工作，program 指成品。

entries.definition: The person who writes the code; it answers who, where program answers what.
entries.definitionCN: 指写代码的人；它回答「谁」，而 program 回答「什么」。

entries.definition: Built on the Greek noun with a Latinised ending: it describes something done by fixed plan, as in programmatic music or programmatic reform.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊名词加拉丁化词尾构成：描述按固定计划进行的事物，如标题音乐或按纲领推行的改革。

entries.definition: The broad intention and the steps meant to reach it; a program is usually a plan that has been written down, funded or scheduled.
entries.definitionCN: 指总体意图及实现它的步骤；program 通常是已写下来、已拨款或已排期的计划。

entries.definition: The arrangement of times and dates; a program may contain a schedule, but a schedule says only when, not what for.
entries.definitionCN: 指时间与日期的安排；program 里可能含 schedule，但时间表只说「何时」，不说「为何」。

entries.definition: Programs and data treated as a product or a body of material; one program is a single unit of software.
entries.definitionCN: 把程序与数据当作产品与整套材料；一个 program 是软件的一个单元。

entries.definition: The list of items to be discussed at a meeting; it is a program for a discussion rather than for a machine or a season.
entries.definitionCN: 会议上要讨论的事项清单；它是讨论的程序，而非机器或演出季的程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek pieces, the real family and the real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek pro- means before and graphein means write, so a program is something written down before it happens.
normal.cn: 希腊语 pro- 意为「在前」，graphein 意为「书写」，所以 program 就是事先写下来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs program, programme, programming, programmer, programmable and programmatic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 program、programme、programming、programmer、programmable 与 programmatic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the plan sense: training program, welfare program, housing program.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示「计划」义：培训计划、福利计划、住房计划。

normal.en: The two spellings differ only in the ending, and computing settles on program everywhere.
normal.cn: 两种拼写只差词尾，计算机领域各地都落在 program 上。

normal.en: The verb splits by object: you program a computer with code, and you program a timer with a setting.
normal.cn: 动词按宾语分工：给计算机编程是写代码，给定时器设程序是调设定。

abstract.en: Picture a playbill that keeps fluttering after the audience has gone, still deciding the order of a night that is over.
abstract.cn: 想象一张观众散场后仍在飘动的节目单，还在决定一个已经结束的夜晚的顺序。

abstract.en: Picture a strip of paper sliding into a machine, and the machine growing a spine as it reads.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸条滑进机器，机器一边读一边长出脊骨。

abstract.en: Picture traffic lights blinking to a timetable nobody in the street can see.
abstract.cn: 想象街上的红绿灯按一张路人看不见的时间表眨眼。

examples.en: A well-written program can be read by another person without running it.
examples.cn: 写得好的程序，别人不运行也能读懂。

examples.en: The museum program lists four lectures and one concert.
examples.cn: 博物馆的活动日程列出四场讲座和一场音乐会。

examples.en: She programmed the irrigation system to water the field before dawn.
examples.cn: 她把灌溉系统设定在黎明前浇水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）来个（gram）」——事先扑上去写下来的东西，就是计划与程序

root: 希腊 pro-「在前」+ graphein「书写」→ programma「公开书面通告」→ 拉丁 programma → 法语 programme → 英语 program；计算机义始于二十世纪四十年代。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one thread: something is written down in advance, first as a notice, then as an order of events, a printed list, a show, a set of machine instructions, a course, a funded scheme, and at last as the act of setting or coding.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一条线索展开：某事被事先写下来，先是通告，再是活动顺序、印刷节目单、播出节目、机器指令集、课程、拨款项目，最后是设定与编程这两个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of times and steps pinned to the wall, with a machine reading the sheet line by line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满时间与步骤的纸钉在墙上，机器一行行读着这张纸。

branches.en: PLAN AND SCHEME: an intention set down in advance, whether a household plan or a funded public scheme.
branches.cn: 计划与方案：事先写下的意图，无论家务安排还是拨款推行的公共项目。

branches.en: TIME ARRANGEMENT: an order of events in time, applied to people and then to devices that must act on cue.
branches.cn: 时间安排：按时间排出的活动顺序，先用于人，后用于必须按时动作的设备。

branches.en: LIST AND SHOW: the printed order becomes a booklet, and the booklet gives its name to the broadcast item.
branches.cn: 节目单与节目：印刷的顺序成为小册子，小册子又把名字让给播出的节目。

branches.en: CODE: the written sequence is now for a machine, first as a noun and then as the verb that puts it there.
branches.cn: 代码：写下的序列改为给机器用，先是名词，再是把序列装进去的动词。

branches.en: COURSE OF STUDY: a degree is also a sequence of steps completed in order, so schools use the same word.
branches.cn: 课程：学位同样是一串按顺序完成的步骤，学校于是沿用同一个词。

intro.en: Program is Greek in its two pieces, Latin in its noun ending and French in its modern shape. English then added -ing, -er and -able to build the computing family.
intro.cn: program 的两个构件来自希腊语，名词词尾来自拉丁语，现代形式来自法语。英语随后加 -ing、-er、-able 构成计算机词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin programma is the one learned borrowing that carries the word from Greek into French and English; the other Latin-looking ending -atic came later through French adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 programma 是把这个词从希腊语带到法语与英语的唯一学术借词；另一个似拉丁的词尾 -atic 是后来经法语形容词进入的。

items.example: The prefix places the writing ahead of the event.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「写」放在事情发生之前。

items.example: The verb names the act of setting marks down.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把符号落下来的动作。

items.example: The ending turns the act of writing into a written thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「写」这个动作变成「写出来的东西」。

items.example: The Greek noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是整个词族的源头。

items.meaning: a notice; an order of events
items.example: English took the French shape in the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十七世纪接受了法语的形式。

items.meaning: a plan or a coded instruction set
items.example: The short spelling became standard in computing.
items.exampleCN: 短拼写在计算机领域成为标准。

items.example: Programming names the work rather than the product.
items.exampleCN: programming 指这项工作，而不是成品。

items.example: A programmer is the one who writes the code.
A programmable device can hold a new sequence.
items.exampleCN: 可编程设备能装入新的序列。

items.example: Programmatic music follows a written story.
items.exampleCN: 标题音乐遵循一个写好的故事。

senses.title: Forward movement towards a place
senses.definition: movement forward, especially of a group of people or a vehicle towards a destination
senses.definitionCN: 向前移动，尤指人群或车辆朝目的地行进
senses.example: The army's progress through the valley was slowed by rain.
senses.exampleCN: 军队穿过山谷的行进被雨拖慢了。
senses.why: Latin progredi is built from pro-, forward, and gradi, to walk, so the first sense is simply walking forward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 progredi 由 pro-（向前）和 gradi（走）构成，所以最初的意思就是「往前走」。

senses.title: Development towards a better state
senses.definition: the gradual improvement or development of a person, a project or a society
senses.definitionCN: 个人、项目或社会逐渐变好或向前发展
senses.example: She has made real progress in her spoken English.
senses.exampleCN: 她的英语口语有了实实在在的进步。
senses.why: Walking forward easily turns into a metaphor for moving towards a goal, so the word came to mean any step towards something better.
senses.whyCN: 「往前走」很容易被用来比喻「朝目标迈进」，于是这个词就指任何向更好状态靠近的一步。

senses.title: To move forward
senses.definition: to move forward or continue on a course
senses.definitionCN: 向前移动，或沿某条路线继续前行
senses.example: The procession progressed slowly along the narrow street.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍沿着窄街缓慢前行。
senses.why: The verb keeps the literal Latin sense of walking on, and its stress falls on the second syllable, unlike the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语「继续走」的本义，重音落在第二个音节上，与名词不同。

senses.title: To improve or develop
senses.definition: to develop or improve, especially over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里逐渐发展或变好
senses.example: Work on the new school is progressing faster than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 新学校的工程进展比预期更快。
senses.why: Because the noun already meant improvement, the verb took on the same figurative sense and now often describes projects and conditions.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词已经表示「变好」，动词也就承接了这层比喻义，如今多用来描述工程与状况。

intro.en: Progress comes from a Latin verb that joins forward to walk, and the noun keeps the same image of a journey towards something.
intro.cn: progress 出自一个把「向前」和「走」合起来的拉丁动词，名词里仍保留着「朝某处走」的画面。

items.en: The prefix pro- meant forward, and gradi meant to walk or to step, so the two together described stepping onward.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示向前，动词 gradi 表示走、迈步，两者合起来就是「向前迈」。

items.en: Progredi meant to go forward, to advance, and its past participle progressus supplied the noun.
items.cn: progredi 意为前进、推进，其过去分词 progressus 提供了名词形式。

items.en: Progressus named a going forward, both on the ground and in the course of events.
items.cn: progressus 指向前行进，既指脚下的路，也指事情的进程。

items.en: Old French progres kept the noun sense of advance and passed it into English.
items.cn: 古法语 progres 保留「前进」的名词义，并传入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses progress for movement and improvement, and also as a verb; the noun stresses the first syllable and the verb the second.
items.cn: 现代英语用 progress 表示行进与进步，也可作动词；名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin root of stepping; the near-meaning group gathers words for moving and getting better.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「迈步」词根上的词；近义组收表示前行与变好的词。

entries.definition: Moving forward step by step, or favouring social reform.
entries.definitionCN: 一步步向前的；主张社会改革的。

entries.definition: A series of steps or stages in a process.
entries.definitionCN: 过程中的一连串步骤或阶段。

entries.definition: To move backwards to an earlier or worse state.
entries.definitionCN: 退回较早或较差的状态。

entries.definition: Happening slowly, in small steps.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢发生的，一步一步的。

entries.definition: Forward movement, or a step towards a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 向前移动，或朝目标迈出的一步。

entries.definition: The process of growing or becoming more advanced.
entries.definitionCN: 成长或变得更先进的过程。

entries.definition: A change that makes something better.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变好的改变。

entries.definition: Forward movement, especially against difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指克服困难后的前进。

normalIntro.en: The word is a walk turned into a picture of improvement, and its family keeps the same forward step.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把「走路」变成「变好」的比喻，同族词都保留着那一步向前的动作。

normal.en: Latin gradi means to walk, so progress is first a matter of feet, not of grades.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 gradi 意为「走」，所以 progress 最初说的是脚步，而不是分数。

normal.en: The prefix pro- points forward, which is why progress always carries a direction.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 指向前方，所以 progress 总带着方向感。

normal.en: The noun puts the beat on the first syllable and the verb on the second, as English often does with such pairs.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节，英语里这类成对的词常常如此。

normal.en: Progressive adds -ive: a person or policy that keeps moving forward.
normal.cn: progressive 加 -ive，指不断向前的人或政策。

normal.en: Progression adds -ion: the series of steps that a forward movement leaves behind.
normal.cn: progression 加 -ion，指前进过程中留下的一连串步骤。

abstract.en: A journey and an improvement share one word because both are measured by where you were and where you are.
abstract.cn: 旅程和进步共用一个词，因为两者都要靠「原来在哪、现在在哪」来衡量。

abstract.en: Progress is invisible in a single moment; it only appears when you look back at the distance covered.
abstract.cn: 进度在单独一刻里看不见，只有回头看走过的距离时才显现。

abstract.en: The same word can be a thing and an action, which is why English can say that progress progresses.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能是事物也能是动作，所以英语里可以说 progress 自己在前行。

examples.en: She has made real progress in her spoken English.
examples.cn: 她的英语口语有了实实在在的进步。

examples.en: The procession progressed slowly along the narrow street.
examples.cn: 队伍沿着窄街缓慢前行。

examples.en: Negotiations are still in progress.
examples.cn: 谈判仍在进行中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若格瑞斯」——听着像「扑过去，格外卖力」，往前一扑再使劲，就是进步。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ gradi（走）构成 progredi，过去分词 progressus 意为「向前走」，经古法语 progres 进入英语；名词重音在前，动词重音在后。

sensesIntro.en: The core is walking forward; the senses split into the journey itself, the improvement it stands for, and the two verb uses that follow.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「向前走」；义项分成脚下的行进、由它比喻出的进步，以及随之而来的两种动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group of walkers moving steadily along a ridge, with the ground already covered stretching out behind them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人沿着山脊稳步向前，走过的路在身后越拉越长。

branches.en: a column of walkers rounding a bend
branches.cn: 一队行人绕过弯道

branches.en: a learner reading a page that once looked impossible
branches.cn: 学习者读着一页曾经觉得很难读的文字

branches.en: a river of people moving through a narrow street
branches.cn: 人流沿着窄街向前移动

branches.en: a building site gaining a floor each month
branches.cn: 工地每个月多出一层

branches.en: a project that is visibly further along than last year
branches.cn: 比去年明显推进了的项目

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin prefix of forward movement and a Latin verb of walking, with English endings added later.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示向前的拉丁语前缀和表示行走的拉丁语动词构成，英语后缀是后来加上的。

latinIntro.en: Latin gradi, to walk, and its participle progressus sit behind the English noun and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gradi（走）及其分词 progressus 是英语名词与动词的来源。

definition_zh: 项目；工程；课题；计划；投射；凸出；预测；表现（形象）
definition_en: a planned piece of work, or to throw something forward in space, time, or imagination
core_image: 把一张纸向前抛出去，纸面在空中展开成一块可见的平面
scene: 会议室里，团队把目标、时间线、负责人写在墙上。The whole project is pinned to the wall, with its goals, its timeline and the name of the person who owns each part.
sceneCN: 这里 project 是「项目、工程」（第 1 个义项：为达成目标而规划的一整块工作）；句意：整个项目都贴在墙上，写着目标、时间线，以及每一部分的负责人。图中可辨识物件：项目看板、便利贴、时间线、负责人照片、马克笔；对应第 1 个义项。

投射；凸出；预测；表现（形象）；使（影像）成像

senses.title: A planned piece of work
senses.definition: a planned undertaking with a goal, a timetable, and resources
senses.definitionCN: 有计划、有目标、有时间与资源的任务
senses.example: The bridge project will take five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的工程要五年。
senses.why: Latin proiectum is 'something thrown forward'. A project is a plan thrown ahead of you, a future state you have already sketched.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proiectum 是“被抛向前之物”。project 是被投到你前方的计划，一幅你已勾画出的未来图景。

senses.title: A research or study topic
senses.definition: a specific piece of research or academic work
senses.definitionCN: 一项具体的研究或学术工作
senses.example: She is working on a project about urban birds.
senses.exampleCN: 她在做一个关于城市鸟类的课题。
senses.why: Schools and labs cut knowledge into manageable pieces. Each project is a bounded task with its own question, method, and deadline.
senses.whyCN: 学校与实验室把知识切成可处理的块。每个 project 都是有界任务，有自己的问题、方法与期限。

senses.title: To estimate or forecast
senses.definition: to calculate what a quantity will be in the future
senses.definitionCN: 计算某数量在未来会是多少
senses.example: Analysts project a rise in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师预计需求上升。
senses.why: Forecasting is throwing a number forward in time. The same verb that launches an object through space launches a figure into next year.
senses.whyCN: 预测是把一个数字抛向未来。同一个把物体抛过空间的动词，也把数字抛进明年。

senses.title: To throw forward physically
senses.definition: to throw or cast something forward
senses.definitionCN: 把某物向前抛
senses.example: The machine projects balls at high speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器高速抛出球。
senses.why: This is the literal core: iacere 'to throw' with pro- 'forward'. Every abstract sense is a metaphor built on this physical cast.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：iacere“投”加 pro-“向前”。一切抽象义都建在这个物理抛掷上。

senses.title: To cast an image onto a surface
senses.definition: to cause light or an image to fall on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 使光或影像落在某个表面
senses.example: The device projects the map onto the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 设备把地图投射到墙上。
senses.why: Light is thrown forward and lands on a screen. The projector is the object that throws, and the image is what arrives.
senses.whyCN: 光被抛向前方，落在屏幕上。projector 是抛掷之物，影像则是到达之物。

senses.title: To extend outward
senses.definition: of a part, to stick out beyond the main body
senses.definitionCN: 某部分超出主体向外伸
senses.example: The balcony projects over the street.
senses.exampleCN: 阳台向街道上方凸出。
senses.why: A shape that juts out is literally thrown beyond the wall. Architecture uses the word for any part that advances past its base.
senses.whyCN: 向外突出的形状，字面上被抛出了墙外。建筑学用这个词指任何越过基线的部分。

senses.title: To convey an impression
senses.definition: to communicate a quality or image to others
senses.definitionCN: 向他人传达某种品质或形象
senses.example: A good speaker projects confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 好的演讲者展现自信。
senses.why: Social presence is treated as a projection: an inner state is thrown outward so others can see it. The word implies deliberate display.
senses.whyCN: 社会在场被当作一种投射：内在状态被抛到外面，让他人看见。这个词隐含刻意的展示。

senses.title: To predict by extrapolation
senses.definition: to extend a trend or pattern into the future
senses.definitionCN: 把趋势或模式延伸到未来
senses.example: The model projects growth through 2030.
senses.exampleCN: 模型推算增长将持续到 2030 年。
senses.why: Statistics throws a line forward from known points. Projection is the noun, and it always carries the caveat that the future may not land where the line points.
senses.whyCN: 统计把一条线从已知点向前抛。projection 是名词，且总带着警告：未来未必落在线的落点。

senses.title: To protrude anatomically
senses.definition: of a body part, to stick out from the surface
senses.definitionCN: 身体某部分从表面突出
senses.example: The jaw projects forward.
senses.exampleCN: 下颌向前突出。
senses.why: Bones and features can be thrown beyond the body's outline. Anatomy uses the same spatial verb as architecture, applied to flesh.
senses.whyCN: 骨与特征可以超出身体轮廓。解剖学把与建筑相同的空间动词用于肉体。

senses.title: To map onto a plane (geometry)
senses.definition: to represent a figure on a plane by drawing lines from it
senses.definitionCN: 用射线把图形表示到平面上
senses.example: Project the sphere onto a flat map.
senses.exampleCN: 把球面投影到平面地图上。
senses.why: Geometry formalizes the light image: points are carried along rays to a surface. Map projections keep the same metaphor, with distortion as the price.
senses.whyCN: 几何学把光的意象形式化：点沿射线被带到表面。地图投影保留同一隐喻，代价是变形。

intro.en: Project is a throwing word. Latin proicere joins pro- 'forward' to iacere 'to throw'. A plan, an image, a forecast, and a balcony are all things thrown ahead of the body.
intro.cn: project 是一个抛掷词。拉丁语 proicere 把 pro-“向前”与 iacere“投”结合。计划、影像、预测与阳台，都是被抛到身体前方的东西。

items.en: The noun is first recorded as 'a plan, scheme, design'.
items.cn: 名词最早记录为“计划、方案、设计”。

items.en: From Latin proiectum 'something thrown forth', neuter past participle of proicere 'throw forward' = pro- 'forward' + iacere 'to throw'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 proiectum“被抛向前之物”，是 proicere“向前抛”的中性过去分词 = pro-“向前”+ iacere“投”。

items.en: iacere also gives eject, inject, reject, subject, and object. The family is about throwing, and the prefix sets the direction.
items.cn: iacere 还生成 eject、inject、reject、subject、object。这个词族关乎投掷，前缀定方向。

items.en: The verb appears with the sense 'to throw or cast forward'.
items.cn: 动词出现，义为“向前投掷”。

items.en: Projection extends to optics, psychology (projecting an image), and statistics (projecting a trend).
items.cn: projection 扩展到光学、心理学（投射形象）与统计学（推算趋势）。

items.en: Modern English uses project for both a planned task and the act of throwing an image, a forecast, or a shape forward.
items.cn: 现代英语用 project 既指计划任务，也指把影像、预测或形状向前抛出的动作。

note.en: The first group shares the iacere root and the -ject shape; the second is about words that also mean a plan or a forecast.
note.cn: 第一组共享 iacere 词根与 -ject 形态，第二组看同样表示“计划”或“预测”的词。

entries.definition: the act of projecting; a forecast or a protruding part.
entries.definitionCN: 投射；预测；凸出部分。

entries.definition: a device that throws an image onto a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 把影像投到表面的设备。

entries.definition: to throw back; to refuse. It is re- 'back' + iacere.
entries.definitionCN: 掷回；拒绝。它是 re-“向后”+ iacere。

entries.definition: a detailed proposal for doing something. It emphasizes intention, not the work itself.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的详细提议。它强调意图，而非工作本身。

entries.definition: a statement about what will happen. It matches project sense 3 but is more concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将发生之事的陈述。它对应 project 第 3 义，但更具体。

entries.definition: a risky new business or activity. It stresses risk rather than planning.
entries.definitionCN: 有风险的新事业。它强调风险，而非规划。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin iacere 'throw', the pro- 'forward' prefix, the reject/inject/eject family, and the optics and statistics uses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 iacere“投”、前缀 pro-“向前”、reject/inject/eject 词族，以及光学与统计用法。

normal.en: Iacere means 'throw'; pro- means 'forward'. A project is something thrown ahead of you.
normal.cn: iacere 意为“投”；pro- 意为“向前”。project 是被抛到你前方的东西。

normal.en: Reject throws back, inject throws in, eject throws out, project throws forward: the prefix is the direction.
normal.cn: reject 掷回，inject 掷入，eject 掷出，project 掷向前：前缀就是方向。

normal.en: A projector throws light; a balcony throws itself beyond the wall; a forecast throws a number into next year.
normal.cn: 投影仪抛光；阳台把自己抛出墙外；预测把数字抛进明年。

normal.en: Project management is planning seen as a launched object: it has a target, a trajectory, and a landing date.
normal.cn: 项目管理就是把计划看作被发射的物体：它有目标、弹道与落地日期。

normal.en: Projecting confidence is throwing an inner state outward so others can catch it.
normal.cn: 展现自信，是把内在状态抛到外面，让他人接住。

abstract.en: Planning is projective: to make a project is to live in a future you have already thrown into view.
abstract.cn: 规划是投射性的：做一个项目，就是住在一个已被你抛入视野的未来里。

abstract.en: Every projection distorts: a map, a forecast, and a self-image all flatten something three-dimensional.
abstract.cn: 每一种投影都会变形：地图、预测与自我形象，都把某种立体之物压平。

abstract.en: The word ties action to imagination: what we throw forward is first an object of thought, then a thing in the world.
abstract.cn: 这个词把行动与想象绑在一起：我们抛向前方的，先是思想的对象，然后才是世界中的实物。

examples.en: The team finished the project ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 团队提前完成了项目。

examples.en: The film was projected onto a huge screen.
examples.cn: 影片被投射到一块巨大的屏幕上。

examples.en: Sales are projected to grow by ten percent.
examples.cn: 销售额预计增长百分之十。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若杰克特”——扑向前，像杰克特（飞镖）一样被抛出 → project 项目、投射

root: 拉丁语 proicere“向前抛”= pro-“向前”+ iacere“投”；过去分词 proiectum。同族有 eject、inject、reject、subject。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of project, all one throw. What is thrown can be a plan (a project), an image (a projection), a number (a forecast), a wall (a balcony), or a self (a persona).
sensesIntro.cn: project 的十个义项，都是同一次抛掷。被抛出的可以是计划（项目）、影像（投影）、数字（预测）、墙体（阳台），或自我（形象）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something thrown forward from the body into space or time.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物从身体被抛向前方，进入空间或时间。

branches.en: PLAN: a future task sketched and thrown ahead.
branches.cn: 计划：被勾画并抛向前方的未来任务。

branches.en: CAST: physical throwing, light onto a surface, and geometric projection.
branches.cn: 投射：物理抛掷、光落表面与几何投影。

branches.en: PROTRUDE: a part thrown beyond the outline, in buildings and bodies.
branches.cn: 凸出：在建筑与身体中超出轮廓的部分。

branches.en: PERSONA: an inner state thrown outward for others to see.
branches.cn: 形象：内在状态被抛向外，供他人看见。

branches.en: FORECAST: a number or trend carried into the future.
branches.cn: 预测：被带到未来的数字或趋势。

intro.en: Project is noun and verb. English adds -ion, -or, and -ed, and the root iacere also builds reject, inject, eject, and subject.
intro.cn: project 既是名词也是动词。英语加 -ion、-or、-ed，词根 iacere 还构成 reject、inject、eject、subject。

latinIntro.en: Latin proicere 'throw forward' and its participle proiectum stand beside iacere 'throw'. The -ject family is a set of directions: re- back, in- in, e- out, pro- forward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proicere“向前抛”及其分词 proiectum 旁边是 iacere“投”。-ject 词族是一组方向：re- 向后、in- 向内、e- 向外、pro- 向前。
