definition_zh: 许诺；答应；承诺；诺言；希望；前途
definition_en: to say firmly that one will do something, the statement so made, and the signs that something good is likely to come
core_image: 两只手伸出去一击为定，把一句还看不见的话变成双方都得守住的东西
scene: 临行前，父亲把旧钥匙放进儿子手里，说定秋天一定回来看那棵老树。Before he left, he promised to come back for the harvest.
sceneCN: 这里表示「许诺、答应」（第 1 个义项：明确说出自己一定会做某事）；句意为他在离开之前答应回来参加秋收。

pos.zh: 许诺；答应；有希望
诺言；承诺；希望；前途

derivatives.zh: 由 promise 加 -ing 构成，义为「有前途的；有希望的」
由拉丁词干 promiss- 加 -ory 构成，义为「承诺的；约定的」，常见于法律文书
由 promising 再加 -ly 构成，义为「有希望地；看来不错地」

senses.title: To say firmly that one will do something
senses.definition: to tell someone that you will certainly do something, so that the other person can count on it
senses.definitionCN: 明确告诉某人自己一定会做某事，使对方可以指望
senses.example: She promised to call as soon as she landed.
senses.exampleCN: 她答应一下飞机就打电话。
senses.why: The Latin verb sent a word forward toward the listener, so the act begins as a message travelling out of the speaker's mouth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词的意思是「把话往前送」，所以这个动作起初是一句话从说话人嘴里飞向听者。

senses.title: A statement that one will certainly do something
senses.definition: a statement in which someone says that they will certainly do something
senses.definitionCN: 某人说定自己一定会做某事的说法
senses.example: He kept every promise he made that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那个夏天他许下的每个诺言都守住了。
senses.why: Once spoken, the message no longer belongs to the speaker alone; it can be kept, quoted or thrown back, which is how the verb turns into the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 话一出口就不再只属于说话人，它会被收着、被引用、被拿出来对质；动词就这样变成了那个被送出的东西。

senses.title: To show signs that something good is likely
senses.definition: to give signs that something good or important is likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 显出好结果或重要事情很可能发生的迹象
senses.example: The early sales figures promise a strong year.
senses.exampleCN: 早期销售数字预示着这一年会很不错。
senses.why: A pledge always leans toward a future that has not arrived; when clouds or numbers do the leaning, the word keeps only that forward look and drops the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 诺言本就朝着一个还没到来的将来倾斜；当乌云或数字在倾斜时，这个词只留下「朝前指」的动作，说话人则退场了。

senses.title: The quality of seeming likely to succeed
senses.definition: the quality of seeming likely to succeed, especially in a young person or a new project
senses.definitionCN: 看起来很可能成功的那份质地，尤指年轻人或新项目身上的
senses.example: The young pianist showed promise from her first recital.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻钢琴家从第一场独奏会起就显出前途。
senses.why: If the good thing is promised but has not arrived, the noun can name that waiting good thing directly, and English does so especially for talent that has not yet proved itself.
senses.whyCN: 如果好事已被许诺却还没到，名词就能直接指那件正在等着的好事；英语尤其用它来说尚未证明自己的才华。

intro.en: Promise comes from a Latin verb meaning to send a word forward, and the English word still has the shape of a message flying toward someone who will hold you to it.
intro.cn: promise 来自一个意为「把话往前送」的拉丁动词，这个词至今保持着「一句话飞向对方，对方据此要求你兑现」的形状。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it sits inside many English words about sending and releasing.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放走，是许多表示「送出、释放」的英语词里的那个成分。

items.en: The prefix pro- pushed the sending forward, so promittere meant to send a word forth, that is, to give someone your word.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 把「送」推向前面，于是 promittere 意为把话送出去，也就是向人许下诺言。

items.en: The participle promissum named the thing sent forth rather than the sending, and it is the direct source of the noun.
items.cn: 分词 promissum 指被送出的那个东西，而不是送的动作，是名词义项的直接来源。

items.en: Old French kept the noun as promesse, meaning a pledge, and English borrowed it with the ending reshaped as promise.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词写作 promesse，意为诺言，英语借入时把词尾改成 promise。

items.en: English uses the verb for giving one's word and the noun for the word given, then stretches both to the hopeful signs that point at a good future.
items.cn: 现代英语用动词指给出承诺，用名词指给出的那句话，再把两者扩展到指向美好未来的种种迹象。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of sending, including a legal pair for the two sides of a pledge; the second group gathers words for solemn promises.
note.cn: 第一组共用表示「送出」的拉丁动词，还包括指承诺双方的一对法律用语；第二组收表示郑重许诺的词。

entries.definition: Relating to a promise, especially one that has legal force.
entries.definitionCN: 与承诺有关的，尤指具有法律效力的承诺。

entries.definition: In law, the person to whom a promise is made.
entries.definitionCN: 法律用语，指接受承诺的一方。

entries.definition: In law, the person who makes a promise.
entries.definitionCN: 法律用语，指做出承诺的一方。

entries.definition: A statement assumed true as a basis for reasoning; it shares the Latin verb of sending but not the sense of pledging.
entries.definitionCN: 推理时被当作前提的陈述；与本词共用拉丁「送」动词，但没有许诺之义。

entries.definition: A serious promise, often backed by something given as security.
entries.definitionCN: 郑重的承诺，常以某物作担保。

entries.definition: A solemn promise, especially one about marriage or faith.
entries.definitionCN: 庄严的誓愿，尤指关于婚姻或信仰的。

entries.definition: A formal promise made before a witness or on something sacred.
entries.definitionCN: 在见证人面前或对神圣之物做出的正式承诺。

entries.definition: A statement meant to give someone confidence about the future.
entries.definitionCN: 意在让人对将来安心的说法。

normalIntro.en: Every sense keeps the picture of a word sent forward: someone speaks, the word travels, and the listener is then entitled to expect something.
normalIntro.cn: 每个义项都保留着「一句话被送出去」的画面：有人开口，话飞过去，听的人从此有权期待某件事。

normal.en: Mittere is Latin for to send, and pro- pushes it forward, so promittere is to send a word ahead of you.
normal.cn: mittere 是拉丁语的「送」，pro- 把它往前推，所以 promittere 就是「把话先送出去」。

normal.en: Promissum is the thing that was sent, which is why the noun means the word given and not the act of giving it.
normal.cn: promissum 是被送出的那个东西，所以名词义指说出的那句话，而不是说这句话的动作。

normal.en: Promising adds -ing to describe someone or something that already looks like a coming success.
normal.cn: promising 加 -ing，用来形容已经显出成功样子的年轻人或事物。

normal.en: Weather that promises rain keeps only the forward-pointing part of a pledge, with nobody actually pledging.
normal.cn: 天气 promise rain 只保留了许诺中「朝前指」的那一半，并没有谁真的在许诺。

normal.en: Keep and break fit promise because a pledge is treated like an object held in the hand or dropped on the floor.
normal.cn: keep 与 break 能配 promise，是因为诺言被当成手里的东西：可以握住，也可以摔掉。

abstract.en: A promise is a word lent forward in time, and the debt is settled when that future finally arrives.
abstract.cn: 诺言是一句被借到将来的话，等那个将来真的到来，债才算还清。

abstract.en: One word covers a pledge and a hopeful sign because both are the present pointing at something not yet here.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指誓言，也指好兆头，因为两者都是「现在」在指向尚未到来的东西。

abstract.en: To promise is to make your future self answerable to another person's memory of what you said.
abstract.cn: 许诺就是让你的将来那个自己去面对别人记住的那句话。

examples.en: She promised to send the file before noon.
examples.cn: 她答应中午前把文件发过去。

examples.en: He broke his promise and never mentioned it again.
examples.cn: 他违背了诺言，此后再没提起。

examples.en: The new treatment promises to help patients who failed older drugs.
examples.cn: 这种新疗法有望帮助那些对旧药无效的病人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若米事」——说出口的事像米粒撒出去，收不回来，只能认账；记住 promise 是许诺。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ mittere（送、放出）→ promittere（把话送出去、许下诺言）→ promissum（被送出的承诺），经古法语 promesse 进入英语；同族词多与「送出、放出」有关，premise 与本词共用 mittere，但前缀不同、意义也走远。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a word sent forward to bind the speaker; from it come the pledge itself, the hopeful sign, and the promise that a future holds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「一句被送出去、用来约束说话人的话」；由此分出那句诺言本身、指向好结果的迹象，以及关于前途的希望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands meeting in a hard clasp, turning spoken words into something both sides must keep.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手用力一击，把说出口的话变成双方都得守住的东西。

branches.en: a hand stretched out before the sentence is finished
branches.cn: 话还没说完，手已经伸了出去

branches.en: a written pledge folded away in a drawer
branches.cn: 写下来的承诺折好收进抽屉

branches.en: dark clouds carrying the smell of coming rain
branches.cn: 带着雨意的乌云压在天边

branches.en: a young musician whose future seems already waiting
branches.cn: 前途仿佛已经在前方等着的年轻乐手

branches.en: one word for a vow and for a hope
branches.cn: 同一个词既指誓言，也指希望

intro.en: A Latin verb of sending, its forward prefix, and the endings that turn the message into a noun and an adjective hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「送」的拉丁动词、表示向前的前缀，以及把这句话变成名词与形容词的词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb promittere and its participle promissum are the reliable cognates behind the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 promittere 及其分词 promissum，是英语这个词可靠的同源词。

items.meaning: to send forth a word, to promise
that which is sent forth, a promise

latinEntries.meaning: to send forth a word, to promise

definition_zh: 发音；读作；宣判；正式宣布；断言
definition_en: to make the sound of a word or letter, or to announce something formally and officially
core_image: 嘴唇、舌头和气流一起，把纸上一串字母变成别人听得见的声音
scene: 新生点名时，老师把花名册上的名字一个个念出来，念到某个姓氏时停了一下。She paused to pronounce the unfamiliar surname slowly and clearly.
sceneCN: 这里取「发音、读出来」的意思（第 1 个义项：把词或字母读出声音）；句意为她停下来，把这个不常见的姓氏慢慢地、清楚地读了出来。花名册上那个生僻的姓就是线索。

pos.zh: 发音；读作；宣判；正式宣布；断言

derivatives.zh: 由 pronounce 加 -ment 构成，义为「公告；正式声明」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「明显的；显著的」
由同一拉丁词干的名词 pronuntiatio 经法语进入英语，义为「发音」
在 pronounce 前加表示「错误地」的前缀 mis-，义为「读错」

senses.title: To make the sound of a word or letter
senses.definition: to make the sound of a word, a name or a letter with the voice
senses.definitionCN: 用嗓音发出单词、名字或字母的读音
senses.example: Nobody in the class could pronounce her family name.
senses.exampleCN: 班上没人能读出她的姓。
senses.why: Latin nuntiare meant to announce, and pro- meant forth, so the pair first meant to bring a sound out into the open; the mouth is only the instrument that does it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nuntiare 意为「宣告」，前缀 pro- 意为「向外」，两者合起来本是「把声音送到外面」；嘴巴只是完成这件事的工具，不是词义的起点。

senses.title: To declare something officially
senses.definition: to announce a sentence, a verdict or a decision in a formal and official way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式、官方的方式宣布判决、裁定或决定
senses.example: The judge pronounced a sentence of five years.
senses.exampleCN: 法官宣判五年徒刑。
senses.why: A court does not merely think its decision, it says it aloud, and the announcing half of the Latin word survives exactly there: the sentence takes effect when it is spoken.
senses.whyCN: 法庭的判决不只是想清楚，还要念出来；拉丁词里「宣告」的那一半正好留在这种场合——判词被说出口的那一刻才生效。

senses.title: To state an opinion firmly
senses.definition: to give a firm opinion or judgement about something, often in a slightly formal tone
senses.definitionCN: 对某事给出明确而坚定的看法或评判，语气常偏正式
senses.example: The critic pronounced the film a masterpiece.
senses.exampleCN: 那位影评人断言这部电影是杰作。
senses.why: Anyone who announces a verdict is borrowing a judge's authority, so the word widened from courtrooms to critics and experts who speak as if their view were a ruling.
senses.whyCN: 宣告裁定的人都在借用法官的权威，于是这个词从法庭扩展到评论家和专家身上——他们说话时，仿佛自己的看法就是一条裁定。

senses.title: To be sounded in a particular way
senses.definition: to be sounded in the way described, said of a written word, a name or a letter
senses.definitionCN: 读音如所说的那样，用于说明写出来的单词、名字或字母怎么念
senses.example: The town's name is pronounced with the stress on the first syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇的名字重音落在第一个音节上。
senses.why: English spelling and sound often part company, so the same verb is used passively to record how a written form is actually said, with no declaring involved at all.
senses.whyCN: 英语的拼写和读音常常对不上，于是同一个动词也用被动形式来记录「写出来的形式实际怎么念」，此时完全与「宣告」无关。

intro.en: Pronounce joins a Latin prefix meaning forth to a Latin verb meaning to announce, so the word has always carried both a mouth and a public voice.
intro.cn: pronounce 把表示「向外」的拉丁语前缀接在表示「宣告」的拉丁语动词上，所以这个词从源头起就同时带着「嘴」和「公开的声音」。

items.en: Nuntiare meant to announce, to report or to bring news, and the related noun nuntius meant messenger.
items.cn: nuntiare 意为宣告、报告、带来消息，相关名词 nuntius 指信使。

items.en: Adding pro-, forth, produced pronuntiare, to speak out, to utter, and already to declare in public.
items.cn: 加上表示「向外」的 pro-，得到 pronuntiare，意为说出、发声，并且已经带有「当众宣告」的意味。

items.en: The action noun pronuntiatio named a speaking out and a declaration, and it is the ancestor of the English noun.
items.cn: 动作名词 pronuntiatio 指「说出」与「宣告」，它是英语名词 pronunciation 的祖先。

items.en: Old French softened the consonant cluster and gave the verb as prononcier, with the o of the Latin noun but no t before the ending.
items.cn: 古法语把辅音簇软化，动词写作 prononcier，保有拉丁名词里的 o，但词尾前没有 t。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the verb as pronounce and used it for sounding words and for formal declarations; the noun came separately from the Latin noun, which is why pronunciation has no o.
items.cn: 中古英语借入动词作 pronounce，既用于读词，也用于正式宣告；名词则另从拉丁名词借入，所以 pronunciation 里没有 o。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin verb for announcing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for producing words with the voice.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「宣告」动词上的形式；近义组收用嗓音说出词语的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the way a word is spoken, with no o after the n.
entries.definitionCN: 表示词的读法的名词，n 后面没有 o。

entries.definition: A formal public statement or declaration.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的公开声明或宣告。

entries.definition: To say a word in a wrong way.
entries.definitionCN: 把单词读错。

entries.definition: To make something known publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 公开宣布某事。

entries.definition: To say words clearly and distinctly.
entries.definitionCN: 清晰地咬字发音。

entries.definition: To say something aloud.
entries.definitionCN: 说出；发出（声音）。

entries.definition: To form sounds clearly enough to be understood.
entries.definitionCN: 把音发清楚，使人听得懂。

entries.definition: To state something officially or firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或坚定地声明。

entries.definition: To produce words with the voice.
entries.definitionCN: 用嗓音说出词语。

normalIntro.en: The word holds a mouth and a public voice at once, and its family keeps splitting along those two lines: sounding words, and declaring things.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时握着「嘴」和「公开的声音」，同族词也沿这两条线分开：读词，以及宣告。

normal.en: Latin nuntiare also gives announce, so pronounce and announce are cousins: both bring something out where others can hear it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nuntiare 也带来 announce，所以 pronounce 与 announce 是表亲：两者都把东西送到别人听得见的地方。

normal.en: The prefix pro- means forth, so to pronounce is literally to carry a sound out of the mouth.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示「向外」，所以 pronounce 字面上就是「把声音从嘴里送出去」。

normal.en: The noun pronunciation comes from Latin pronuntiatio, not from the English verb, which is why the o of pronounce is missing there.
normal.cn: 名词 pronunciation 来自拉丁语 pronuntiatio，而不是来自英语动词，所以那里少了 pronounce 的 o。

normal.en: The adjective pronounced means noticeable, because something pronounced has been said out clearly enough to be heard.
normal.cn: 形容词 pronounced 意为「明显的」，因为被清楚说出来的东西自然引人注意。

normal.en: A judge pronounces sentence: the legal use draws on the announcing half of the word, not on the mouth.
normal.cn: 法官宣判用 pronounce sentence，这个法律用法取的是词里「宣告」的那一半，与嘴无关。

abstract.en: A word only becomes fully real when someone pronounces it; print is little more than a set of instructions for the mouth.
abstract.cn: 一个词只有被人念出来才完全成立；纸上的拼写不过是给嘴巴的一套说明。

abstract.en: Saying a verdict and saying a word share one verb because both make something official simply by speaking it.
abstract.cn: 宣读判决和读出一个词共用一个动词，因为两者都只靠「说出来」就让某事生效。

abstract.en: The distance between how a word is written and how it is pronounced is where the history of the language shows through.
abstract.cn: 一个词「怎么写」和「怎么念」之间的距离，正是这门语言的历史露出来的地方。

examples.en: Nobody in the class could pronounce her family name.
examples.cn: 班上没人能读出她的姓。

examples.en: The judge pronounced a sentence of five years.
examples.cn: 法官宣判五年徒刑。

examples.en: The town's name is pronounced with the stress on the first syllable.
examples.cn: 这个镇的名字重音落在第一个音节上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若闹恩斯」——像「扑上去念」，凑到字母跟前使劲念，就是发音。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向外）+ nuntiare（宣告）构成 pronuntiare，本义「说出、当众宣告」；动词经古法语 prononcier 进入英语作 pronounce，名词则另从拉丁语 pronuntiatio 借入。

sensesIntro.en: The core is sending a sound outward; from it grow the mouth's work of saying words, the courtroom's spoken verdict, the expert's spoken judgement, and the passive record of how a written form sounds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把声音送出去」；由它长出嘴读词的动作、法庭上念出的判词、专家说出的定论，以及被动记录「写出来的形式怎么念」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lips, tongue and breath turning a line of printed letters into sound that other people can hear.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴唇、舌头和气流一起，把纸上一行字母变成别人听得见的声音。

branches.en: a teacher pointing at one letter on the board
branches.cn: 老师指着黑板上的一个字母

branches.en: a name written one way and said another
branches.cn: 写法一种、读法另一种的名字

branches.en: a courtroom where the sentence is read aloud
branches.cn: 宣读判词的法庭

branches.en: a critic closing a programme with a verdict
branches.cn: 影评人用一句定论结束节目

branches.en: words spoken as if they were final
branches.cn: 说得像终审一样的话

intro.en: A Latin prefix of outward movement and a Latin verb of announcing hold the word together, and French reshaped the verb before English took it.
intro.cn: 表示向外运动的拉丁语前缀和表示宣告的拉丁语动词共同支撑这个词，法语先在中间改造了动词形式，英语随后借入。

latinIntro.en: Latin nuntiare, to announce, and its compound pronuntiare, to speak out, are the direct sources of the English verb and of its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nuntiare（宣告）及其复合形式 pronuntiare（说出）是英语动词与名词的直接来源。

items.meaning: to sound a word, to declare

definition_zh: 发音；读音；口音；语音
definition_en: the way in which a word or a language is spoken, or a person's way of speaking
core_image: 一个词从纸上站起来，被嘴巴念成一段有重音、有长短的声音
scene: 语言课上，老师让学生把同一个单词读三遍，注意词尾那一点细微的差别。Her pronunciation of the final consonant still sounded slightly French.
sceneCN: 这里取「读音、发音方式」的意思（第 1 个义项：一个词被说出来的声音形式）；句意为她对词尾辅音的读法仍带着一点法语味道。老师反复提醒的那个词尾就是线索。

pos.zh: 发音；读音；口音；语音

derivatives.zh: 来自同一拉丁词干的动词，义为「发音；宣判」
在 pronunciation 前加表示「错误地」的前缀 mis-，义为「读错；错误发音」
由 pronounce 加 -able 与否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「念不出来的」

senses.title: The way a word or language is spoken
senses.definition: the way in which a particular word or language is spoken, including its sounds, stress and rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 某个词或某门语言被说出来的方式，包括音素、重音与节奏
senses.example: The dictionary gives two pronunciations for that word.
senses.exampleCN: 词典给这个词标了两种读音。
senses.why: The Latin noun pronuntiatio named the act of speaking out, and English borrowed that noun rather than the verb, so the word begins from the spoken form and not from the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 pronuntiatio 本指「说出来的动作」，英语借的是这个名词而不是动词，所以这个词的起点是「说出来的声音形式」，不是纸上的拼写。

senses.title: A person's way of speaking
senses.definition: the way a particular person speaks, especially as a sign of where they grew up or learned the language
senses.definitionCN: 某个人说话的方式，尤指能看出其成长地或学语言经历的特征
senses.example: His pronunciation betrayed that he had grown up abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他的口音暴露出他是在国外长大的。
senses.why: If the word names the sound of a whole language, it can also name the sound of one speaker, and in that shift it quietly takes over the work of the word accent.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指整门语言的声音，也就能指某一个说话人的声音；在这一转之中，它悄悄接手了 accent 的工作。

senses.title: Speech sounds as a subject to teach
senses.definition: the part of language teaching that deals with sounds, stress and intonation
senses.definitionCN: 语言教学中处理音素、重音与语调的那一部分内容
senses.example: She teaches pronunciation to adult learners.
senses.exampleCN: 她给成年学员上语音课。
senses.why: Once the sounds of a language can be described, marked and corrected, they become something that can be taught, which is why the word also names a subject on a timetable.
senses.whyCN: 一门语言的声音一旦能被描述、标注、纠正，就成了可以教的东西，所以这个词也指课表上的一门内容。

intro.en: Pronunciation comes straight from a Latin action noun for speaking out, and that is the reason its spelling differs from the verb it seems to belong to.
intro.cn: pronunciation 直接来自一个表示「说出」的拉丁动作名词，这正是它的拼写与看似对应的动词不一致的原因。

items.en: Nuntiare meant to announce or report, and it supplied the announcing core of the whole family.
items.cn: nuntiare 意为宣告、报告，为整族词提供了「宣告」这个核心。

items.en: With the prefix pro-, forth, the verb pronuntiare meant to speak out, to utter sounds and to declare.
items.cn: 加上表示「向外」的前缀 pro-，动词 pronuntiare 意为说出、发声、宣告。

items.en: The noun pronuntiatio named the act and manner of speaking out, and its stem pronuntiat- is what English kept.
items.cn: 名词 pronuntiatio 指说出的动作与方式，英语保留的正是它的词干 pronuntiat-。

items.en: Old French passed the noun on as prononciation, turning the Latin t before i into a soft c sound.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 prononciation，拉丁语里 i 前的 t 变成了软音 c。

items.en: English fixed the spelling as pronunciation with n-u-n, following the Latin stem; the o of pronounce never entered, because this word came from the noun, not the verb.
items.cn: 英语按拉丁词干把拼写固定为带 n-u-n 的 pronunciation；pronounce 里的 o 从未进入，因为这个词来自名词而非动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin noun of speaking out; the near-meaning group gathers words about accent, clarity and the sound of speech.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「说出」名词上的形式；近义组收关于口音、清晰度与语音的词语。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to sound a word or to declare something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示读出一个词或宣布某事的动词。

entries.definition: A wrong way of saying a word.
entries.definitionCN: 读错的发音。

entries.definition: A formal public statement.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的公开声明。

entries.definition: An announcement, especially a solemn one.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告，尤指庄重的宣告。

entries.definition: The way people from a place or group speak.
entries.definitionCN: 某地或某群体说话的腔调。

entries.definition: The clear production of speech sounds.
entries.definitionCN: 语音的清晰发出。

entries.definition: The clarity with which words are spoken or sung.
entries.definitionCN: 说话或演唱时咬字的清晰程度。

entries.definition: The rise and fall of the voice in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 说话时嗓音的升降。

normalIntro.en: The word is a mouth shaping a word into sound, and its memories sit on the Latin noun, on stress, and on the missing letter.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一张嘴把一个词念成声音，记忆点落在拉丁名词、重音，以及那个消失的字母上。

normal.en: The verb has an o after the n and the noun does not, because the noun came from Latin pronuntiatio while the verb came through French prononcier.
normal.cn: 动词在 n 后面有 o，名词没有，因为名词来自拉丁语 pronuntiatio，动词则经法语 prononcier 传来。

normal.en: The -tion ending marks a noun of action, exactly as in declaration and explanation.
normal.cn: -tion 结尾标明这是一个动作名词，就像 declaration 与 explanation 一样。

normal.en: Stress falls late, on the syllable that carries -ation, so the first syllables stay light and quick.
normal.cn: 重音落在后面带 -ation 的音节上，前面几个音节因此又轻又快。

normal.en: Mispronunciation adds mis-, wrongly, and keeps the full Latin stem, so the n-u-n stays visible.
normal.cn: mispronunciation 加上表示「错误地」的 mis-，并保留完整的拉丁词干，所以 n-u-n 清楚可见。

normal.en: Annunciation and announce share the announcing root, so this family is not only about mouths.
normal.cn: annunciation 与 announce 共享「宣告」词根，可见这一族词并不只关乎嘴。

abstract.en: Pronunciation is the part of a word that a dictionary can only approximate; the mouth always finishes the job.
abstract.cn: 发音是词典只能大致描摹的那一部分，最后的成品总要由嘴巴完成。

abstract.en: A word can be spelled one way and spoken another, and the gap between the noun and the verb is a small monument to that fact.
abstract.cn: 词可以这样写、那样念，名词与动词之间的那点差别，正是这件事留下的一个小纪念碑。

abstract.en: To judge someone by their pronunciation is to hear history, geography and family gathered into a single vowel.
abstract.cn: 凭发音判断一个人，等于从一个元音里听出历史、地理与家庭。

examples.en: The dictionary gives two pronunciations for that word.
examples.cn: 词典给这个词标了两种读音。

examples.en: His pronunciation betrayed that he had grown up abroad.
examples.cn: 他的口音暴露出他是在国外长大的。

examples.en: She teaches pronunciation to adult learners.
examples.cn: 她给成年学员上语音课。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若难西」——念着就觉得有点难，越难越要练，正是发音。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向外）+ nuntiare（宣告）构成 pronuntiare，其动作名词 pronuntiatio（说出、宣告）经古法语 prononciation 进入英语；词干保留 n-u-n，所以拼写里没有 pronounce 的 o。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the spoken shape of a word; the senses divide into the sound of a word, the sound of a speaker, and the sound of a language as something to be taught.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一个词被说出来的声音形状」；义项分成一个词的读音、一个说话人的口音，以及作为教学对象的一门语言的语音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a printed word lifted off the page and shaped by the mouth into a stretch of sound with its own beat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个印在纸上的词脱离纸面，被嘴巴塑造成一段有自己节拍的声音。

branches.en: two pronunciations printed side by side in a dictionary
branches.cn: 词典里并排印出的两种读音

branches.en: a familiar word said in an unfamiliar voice
branches.cn: 熟悉词被陌生嗓音读出

branches.en: a listener guessing where a stranger grew up
branches.cn: 听者猜陌生人是在哪里长大的

branches.en: a classroom drilling one difficult consonant
branches.cn: 课堂上反复练一个难辅音

branches.en: a recording played again to catch a single sound
branches.cn: 为听清一个音再放一遍录音

intro.en: A Latin verb of announcing and the action noun built from it hold the word together; French softened the consonants and English kept the Latin stem in the spelling.
intro.cn: 表示宣告的拉丁语动词及其动作名词共同支撑这个词；法语软化了辅音，英语则在拼写上保留了拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin nuntiare, to announce, its compound pronuntiare, and the action noun pronuntiatio are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nuntiare（宣告）、其复合形式 pronuntiare 以及动作名词 pronuntiatio 是英语这个词的直接来源。
